summary: Literature sweep + adversarial novelty check for TI2Net upgrade ideas

verdicts.name: Nuisance-explained identity drift

closest_works.title: Unsupervised Multimodal Deepfake Detection Using Intra- and Cross-Modal Inconsistencies (Tian, Khayatkhoei, Mathai, AbdAlmageed)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Read the full text. Its theory (I(Vg;Y) <= I(Vg;M) + H(Y|M)) says that facial motion and identity are dependent, so a generator must either break identity consistency or distort motion. It shows on VoxCeleb2 that motion predicts identity, and that this motion-identity dependence is broken in fakes. Its intra-modal identity AUC rises with motion magnitude (Fig. 4). It trains on real videos only with AdaFace fine-tuned plus a transformer, and scores the percentile of a T x T identity self-similarity matrix. This is the strongest conceptual precedent for 'identity change must be read relative to motion'.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It never conditions identity drift on motion or pose. The identity score is unconditioned window-to-window similarity. Motion is used only as a cross-modal (audio-lip) check and as a post-hoc stratification variable. It does not regress expected embedding change from pose, expression or quality change, and it computes no residual. It does not cite TI2Net.

closest_works.title: Unmasking Puppeteers: Leveraging Biometric Leakage to Expose Impersonation in AI-based Videoconferencing (NeurIPS 2025)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Read the method. The paper states that pose and expression variance swamps the identity signal (Fig. 3: different identities at the same pose are often closer than the same identity across expressions). It removes that variance explicitly with a pose-conditioned large-margin contrastive loss, using hard negatives of a different identity rendered at the same pose. An LSTM fuses per-frame scores, and extreme-yaw filtering adds AUC (0.929 to 0.966, with a peak at +/-18 deg).
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It learns an invariant embedding and does not predict the expected embedding change and keep the residual. Its input is codec pose-expression latents, not ArcFace on RGB. It needs a reference portrait, and its task is puppeteering, not real vs fake. The ablation 'replace contrastive loss with simple similarity regression' drops AUC to 0.788. That is a regression of similarity, not of nuisance-explained change, but a reviewer will read it as weak evidence against regression-style designs.

closest_works.title: Detecting Deepfake Talking Heads from Facial Biometric Anomalies (Norman & Farid)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Read the full text. It is reference-free and uses the distribution of all-pairs ArcFace cosine similarity within a video, summarized by 9 moments and classified with XGBoost. Pose is handled by discarding frames with pitch/yaw/roll above 25/20/20 deg. The authors speculate that the low-similarity tail in fakes comes from 'complex poses, lighting, or expressions'.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It handles nuisance only by hard gating and has no conditional model of expected drift. It is order-free and has no temporal model. Cross-dataset FaceFusion to CDF-v2 is at chance (48.3% acc), which is exactly the failure Idea A claims to fix.

closest_works.title: Critical Contour Prior-Guided Graph Learning With Pose Calibration for Identity-Aware Deepfake Detection (CP-GAT)
closest_works.exact_overlap: From the abstract: it explicitly says identity-consistency detectors degrade under head-pose variation. It adds a rotation-compensation block trained with pose-calibrated contrastive learning toward frontal faces, then scores identity similarity against references.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It is reference-based and uses frontalization (invariance), not a temporal residual of FR drift unexplained by pose, expression or quality. Read at abstract level only.

closest_works.title: Exploring Static-Dynamic ID Matching and Temporal Static ID Inconsistency for Generalizable Deepfake Detection
closest_works.exact_overlap: From the abstract: reference-free, with a TI2Net-style temporal static-ID anomaly branch plus a branch checking that appearance ID matches behaviour (dynamic) ID. It explicitly targets TI2Net's reenactment weakness.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: Behaviour is a second identity cue that is checked for agreement. It is not an explanatory covariate whose predicted effect on the FR embedding is subtracted. Read at abstract level only.

closest_works.title: CUPID: Reconstructing UV Texture Maps for Interpretable Person-of-Interest Deepfake Detection
closest_works.exact_overlap: Read the method. It factors out pose and expression by 3DMM UV canonicalization and trains on real videos only. Its interpretability map M(T) = U(T) - U(R) subtracts the reference-only displacement distribution, so it shows only the deviation not already explained by natural intra-reference variability (pose-dependent texture artifacts, illumination).
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It is reference/POI-based. Nuisance is removed by geometric canonicalization, not by learning the mapping from nuisance change to embedding change. Normalization is by unconditional intra-reference spread, not conditional on the nuisance values in the test clip.

closest_works.title: Can a World Model Predict a Deepfake Video? A Consistency Margin Prior for Deepfake Detection (ConsistencyNet)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Read the method. It uses the prediction residual r = B(predictor(context)) - sg(encoder(target)) of a natural-video predictor (V-JEPA 2.1 + LoRA) as the forgery signal, with a margin prior ||r_fake|| > ||r_real||. Trained on FF++: CDF-v2 90.5 AUC, DFDC 87.1. This is the generic 'expected vs observed, score the residual' template, applied to video latents and published one week before today.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It predicts generic visual latents from temporal context, not FR-embedding change from explicit nuisance factors. It has no identity, pose, expression or quality conditioning. It is supervised on FF++ fakes.

closest_works.title: ExposeAnyone: Personalized Audio-to-Expression Diffusion Models Are Robust Zero-Shot Face Forgery Detectors
closest_works.exact_overlap: Per the sweep summary (not re-read): real-only conditional model (audio to FLAME expression), with the forgery score being how badly the conditional prediction explains the observation. Its clip-shared 3DMM shape fit disentangles shape from expression.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: The conditioning is audio and the target is expression, and it is reference/POI-personalized. It does not predict FR identity-embedding drift from pose, expression or quality.

closest_works.title: MOTIF: Person-of-Interest Deepfake Detection Beyond 3DMM Coefficients
closest_works.exact_overlap: Per the sweep summary (seen in search, not re-read): per-frame 3DDFA-V3 pose/expression/shape over time, real-only training, whitened scoring against reference variance. Its finding that per-frame shape absorbs expression is a direct threat to using 3DMM deltas as clean nuisance regressors.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It is reference-based, uses no FR embeddings, and does no nuisance-to-identity-drift regression.

closest_works.title: Robust Deepfake Detection for Electronic Know Your Customer Systems Using Registered Images
closest_works.exact_overlap: An explicit TI2Net extension (TDC + registered-image ADC, CE + triplet + anchor-positive). Swapping to AdaFace/WebFace12M lifts CDF from 50.8 to 75.9. A quality-robust backbone is the cheap way to suppress quality-induced false drift.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It does no explicit nuisance estimation or residual modelling, and it needs a registered reference image.

closest_works.title: Predicting Face Recognition Performance Using Image Quality (Dutta, Veldhuis, Spreeuwers)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Adjacent field (biometrics), seen via search. It models FR genuine/impostor similarity distributions conditioned on quality features such as pose and illumination. This is the 'expected similarity given nuisance' half of Idea A in recognition.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: No temporal or forensic use, and it predicts performance rather than scoring per-frame residuals.

closest_works.title: Pose-Robust Face Recognition via Deep Residual Equivariant Mapping (DREAM)
closest_works.exact_overlap: A yaw-gated learned residual in FR feature space, i.e. a learned model of how the embedding shifts with pose (from the sweep; not re-read).
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It is canonicalization for recognition, with no temporal residual scoring and no forensics.

closest_works.title: Dynamic Difference Learning With Spatio-Temporal Correlation for Deepfake Video Detection
closest_works.exact_overlap: From the abstract: it explicitly separates inter-frame differences caused by facial motion from those caused by manipulation, and removes motion-induced differences before modelling inconsistency.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It works at pixel/feature-map level with attention and denoising. It does not use identity embeddings or explicit pose, expression or quality estimates, and has no regression of expected change.

verdicts.remaining_novel_delta:
After about 12 distinct searches (alphaXiv, SciSpace and web) and full-text reads of the closest works, I found no paper that does the specific mechanism. That mechanism is reference-free and works on one video:
1. Estimate per-frame nuisance (head pose, 3DMM expression, illumination, quality/blur).
2. Learn on real videos only a conditional model E[Δi_t | Δn_t, n_t] of the change in a frozen face-recognition embedding, ideally with heteroscedastic variance Σ(n_t).
3. Use the standardized residual of identity drift over time as the forgery signal, either on its own or as input to the TI2Net GRU.

Every close paper differs on at least one axis:
- Prior deepfake works either gate (Norman & Farid), learn invariance (Puppeteers, CP-GAT), canonicalize (CUPID), use behaviour as a second identity that must agree (A&B, She et al. 2024, ID-Reveal), or predict generic latents (ConsistencyNet).
- Face-recognition works (DREAM, Dutta et al.) model nuisance-dependent embedding shift but never as a temporal forensic residual.

Concrete deltas that remain defensible:
(a) A conditional, heteroscedastic 'explained vs unexplained identity drift' decomposition for FR embeddings, trained real-only.
(b) An interpretable per-frame residual that says which drift cannot be explained by pose, expression or quality.
(c) A measured reduction of false positives on high-motion, low-quality real videos. This is the clearest testable claim and none of the prior works reports it.
(d) A possible reenactment angle: following Tian et al.'s theory, residual identity drift that is correlated with expression (driver-identity leakage) may expose Face2Face/NeuralTextures. This is untested and must be shown empirically.

The delta is narrow: novelty lies in the mechanism and formulation, not in the signal.
verdicts.recommended_reframing:
Do not pitch this as 'identity inconsistency robust to pose' or as a new cue; that framing is taken.

Pitch it as a conditional-residual test: 'Nuisance-Explained Identity Dynamics: separating natural identity-embedding drift from forgery drift with a real-only conditional model.' Formulate it explicitly as contextual anomaly detection with heteroscedastic calibration: the residual divided by the predicted σ(pose, expression, quality).

Make the headline claims measurable:
1. False-positive reduction on real videos stratified by motion, pose and quality bins. Use FF++ real, CDF real, DFD real, and VoxCeleb2 or DeepSpeak real, and report FPR at fixed TPR per bin.
2. Cross-dataset gains over TI2Net (DFD 72.0, DFo 76.1, CDF1 66.7, CDF2 68.2).
3. Analysis of residual drift that is correlated with expression on reenactment data (Face2Face, NeuralTextures).

Mandatory controls, without which a reviewer will reject:
(i) TI2Net with AdaFace, MagFace or WebFace12M backbones, to isolate the quality-nuisance effect from the backbone effect.
(ii) TI2Net with pose/quality gating, as in Norman & Farid and Puppeteers.
(iii) TI2Net with nuisance deltas concatenated as extra GRU inputs. This is the 'just give the network the covariates' baseline; the residual must beat it.
(iv) TI2Net on DREAM-normalized or UV-canonicalized embeddings.
(v) A pose-matched-negative contrastive variant, as in Puppeteers.
(vi) A decorrelation check showing that the nuisance regressor cannot predict identity, for example with a clip-shared 3DMM shape following ExposeAnyone/MOTIF, or by verifying that the residual still separates different identities.

Also report the per-frame residual as an interpretability output, and give honest results on reenactment.

verdicts.name: Multi-scale identity self-similarity

closest_works.title: Unsupervised Multimodal Deepfake Detection Using Intra- and Cross-Modal Inconsistencies (Tian, Khayatkhoei, Mathai, AbdAlmageed)
closest_works.exact_overlap: I read the method. It builds an explicit T x T temporal self-similarity matrix of face-identity embeddings (AdaFace, plus a transformer over fixed time windows, fine-tuned with an intra-modal contrastive loss) for reference-free deepfake detection. The score is the n-th percentile of that matrix. Its Fig. 4 shows real versus deepfake identity similarity matrices, the same visual argument Idea B would make. It also gives an information-theoretic argument (an identity-motion trade-off) for why face-swap and reenactment must leak identity inconsistency, and shows that identity-matrix AUC rises with motion magnitude.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It uses a single temporal scale (a fixed window), and the matrix is reduced to a percentile scalar rather than read by a learned 2D CNN or transformer. It has no multi-lag or time-gap channels, no geodesic velocity or acceleration, is not trained with real and fake labels, and has no FF++ to CDF/DFD protocol (evaluation is FakeAVCeleb and KoDF). On FakeAVCeleb its identity-only AUC is 77.9.

closest_works.title: Detecting Deepfake Talking Heads from Facial Biometric Anomalies (Norman and Farid)
closest_works.exact_overlap: I read the method. It takes per-frame ArcFace 512-D embeddings and the cosine similarity of all N(N-1)/2 frame pairs, i.e. the full identity TSM. It is reference-free and targets face-swap and lip-sync. It shows real videos give tight pairwise-similarity distributions while face-swaps give bimodal or broad ones. It also explicitly invites 'more sophisticated approaches' over the same signal.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It treats the matrix as an unordered bag: 9 moments or quantiles plus XGBoost, with no time ordering, lag or time-gap structure, no learned 2D model, and no velocity or acceleration. It needs at least 2000 frames to work well and fails cross-dataset (FaceFusion to CDF-v2 is 48.3% accuracy). It does not cite TI2Net.

closest_works.title: ATSS: Detecting AI-Generated Videos via Anomalous Temporal Self-Similarity
closest_works.exact_overlap: I read the method. It builds T x T cosine TSMs of frozen per-frame embeddings (BLIP-2 visual, caption-text and cross-modal). Each matrix is fed row-wise as T frame tokens to a dedicated Transformer encoder, then fused by cross-attention and classified by an MLP with CE loss. It claims to be 'the first to explicitly operationalize anomalous temporal self-similarity as a discriminative fingerprint'. This is exactly the 'TSM to transformer for forensic real/fake' mechanism of Idea B.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: Its signal is generic scene and semantic features, not face identity, and its setting is T2V/I2V generation, not face swap or reenactment. It uses plain cosine similarity with no geodesic distance, no multi-stride or lag channels, no explicit time-gap encoding beyond row order, and no velocity or acceleration. Its hypothesis also runs the opposite way to Idea B's: fakes are too self-similar, whereas face-swaps are less identity-self-similar.

closest_works.title: Compressed Deepfake Video Detection Based on 3D Spatiotemporal Trajectories
closest_works.exact_overlap: I read the method. It applies time-delay embedding to per-frame facial expression and head-pose features and builds a recurrence plot (a binary all-pairs L1 state-similarity matrix). The plot is converted to an adjacency matrix and classified with a lightweight 2-layer Transformer, on face deepfakes (FF++ HQ/LQ, CDF, DFDC). It explicitly argues for first-frame-to-every-later-frame relations over adjacent-frame differences.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: Its signal is geometric facial motion and head pose, not identity embeddings. The recurrence is binary-thresholded L1, not continuous angular. There are no multi-lag channels or time-gap encoding and no hyperspherical velocity or acceleration. The evaluation is intra-dataset with an 8:1:1 split, not cross-dataset.

closest_works.title: TI2Net: Temporal Identity Inconsistency Network for Deepfake Detection
closest_works.exact_overlap: I read it. Fig. 1 is literally a pairwise ArcFace identity-similarity matrix between frames, real in the lower triangle and fake in the upper. The paper says 'an intuitive solution would be to measure the similarities between identity features' across frames. Table 6 shows that random, spread-out sampling (long gaps) beats sliding windows (CDF2 68.2 vs 50.9) because adjacent-frame differences are near zero, which already hints at long-lag structure.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: The model itself uses only lag-1 Euclidean differences, a GRU last state and triplet loss. It never feeds the matrix to the model, and has no multi-lag, geodesic or second-order terms.

closest_works.title: Counting Out Time: Class Agnostic Video Repetition Counting in the Wild (RepNet)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Canonical source of the 'per-frame embeddings to TSM bottleneck to conv plus transformer' architecture. Idea B's learner over the TSM is architecturally RepNet's.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It is not forensic and has no identity features, geodesic distance or multi-lag design.

closest_works.title: AI-Generated Video Detection via Perceptual Straightening (ReStraV)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Stepwise distance (velocity) and curvature (angle between successive displacements) of a per-frame embedding trajectory as forensic features. This is the 'velocity/acceleration on the embedding trajectory' component. I verified it via the ATSS related-work section and the sweep summary.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It uses Euclidean DINOv2 space, not geodesic geometry on the identity hypersphere, has no TSM and no identity, and targets AIGV.

closest_works.title: Exploiting Style Latent Flows for Generalizing Deepfake Video Detection (StyleFlow/StyleGRU)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Same paradigm as TI2Net (differences of a frozen face latent, GRU, contrastive or triplet loss). Per the sweep, its supplementary already ablates 2nd-order differencing and finds no gain.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It has no TSM, no multi-lag, no geodesic geometry and no identity encoder (it uses pSp StyleGAN latents).

closest_works.title: Towards Robust DeepFake Detection under Unstable Face Sequences (LR-GCN)
closest_works.exact_overlap: All-pairs cross-frame affinity matrix as the core structure for face-forgery video detection (FF++, CDF2, DFDC). Taken from the sweep summary; not re-read.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It uses appearance CNN features, not identity, and is deliberately order-free, the opposite of Idea B's time-gap encoding. The matrix is processed by a GCN, not a 2D learner over the TSM.

closest_works.title: Robust Deepfake Detection for eKYC Systems Using Registered Images
closest_works.exact_overlap: The direct 'TI2Net upgrade' competitor. It shows a stronger face-recognition backbone (AdaFace on WebFace12M) matters enormously, and its retrained TI2Net baselines are useful.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It needs a reference image, uses only lag-1 differences, and has no TSM.

verdicts.strongest_refutation: Every ingredient of Idea B is already published, and the two closest papers sit on the exact signal. (1) Tian et al. 2023/24 (arXiv 2311.17088) already compute a T x T temporal self-similarity matrix of face-recognition identity embeddings for reference-free deepfake detection, plot real-vs-fake identity TSMs, and score the matrix. (2) Norman and Farid 2025 (arXiv 2507.08917) already use the full ArcFace all-pairs cosine matrix of a video as the detection signal for face-swap and lip-sync. (3) TI2Net itself draws the pairwise identity similarity matrix in Fig. 1 and argues for measuring all-pair similarities, so 'use the matrix TI2Net plotted' reads as an obvious next step. (4) ATSS (arXiv 2604.04029, Apr 2026) already claims to be first at the 'TSM of frozen per-frame embeddings, row tokens into a Transformer, real/fake' mechanism. Chen et al. 2024 (arXiv 2404.18149) already feed an all-pairs recurrence plot of facial-motion features to a Transformer on FF++/CDF/DFDC. RepNet is the architectural template. (5) Velocity and curvature of an embedding trajectory (ReStraV, D3) and second-order differencing of face latents (StyleFlow supplementary, reportedly no gain) are prior art. TI2Net's own Table 6 already shows long-gap sampling beats adjacent frames, which anticipates the multi-lag motivation. A harsh area chair would summarise Idea B as 'RepNet/ATSS applied to TI2Net's Fig. 1 matrix': an incremental combination whose individual parts all have citations. Geodesic (arccos) instead of cosine is a monotone reparameterisation of the same matrix, and would be dismissed as cosmetic unless shown to matter empirically.
verdicts.remaining_novel_delta: After reading the closest works and running 10+ extra searches (alphaXiv, SciSpace, web), I found no paper that combines the following. (a) An explicit, time-ordered identity TSM (frozen face-recognition embeddings) used as the input of a learned 2D CNN or transformer encoder and trained supervised with real and fake labels on the FF++ to CDF/DFD/DFDC cross-dataset protocol. Tian et al. use a percentile and Norman and Farid use order-free moments plus XGBoost; ATSS learns over a TSM but of generic BLIP-2 features for AIGV. (b) Multi-lag or stride-indexed channels (lags 1 to 32), i.e. the diagonals or banded views of the identity TSM with explicit time-gap encoding, so the model can separate short-range jitter (frame-wise generator flicker) from long-range drift (pose- or expression-induced identity leakage, the reenactment failure mode). (c) Geodesic first- and second-order identity dynamics on the hypersphere (log-map velocity, parallel-transported acceleration), as opposed to Euclidean differences in TI2Net and StyleFlow or DINOv2 curvature in ReStraV. Individually, (b) is the most defensible piece and (c) the weakest. The defensible claim is therefore narrow: a lag-structured, learned reading of the identity self-similarity matrix beats both lag-1 differencing (TI2Net) and order-free all-pairs statistics (Norman and Farid, Tian et al.), especially on reenactment (Face2Face, NeuralTextures) and long-gap sampling. Whether this delta survives depends entirely on empirical gains and clean ablations.

verdicts.name: Real-only identity dynamics + synthetic identity-jitter

closest_works.title: UniForensics: Face Forgery Detection via General Facial Representation (Dynamic Video Self-Blending, DVSB)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Verified in the method section (Sec. III-C, Eqs. 1-8). It samples every SBI parameter group K(t) per frame (colour, quality, blend dislocation, mask, mask deformation, blur/blend strategy). The white-noise sequence is then Gaussian-filtered in the DCT domain with power preserved, so the forgery strength varies smoothly over time. Pseudo-fake videos are built from real videos only (FF++ real plus VoxCeleb2). Table V ablates the jitter spectrum: static 87.6, independent 86.8, dynamic high-frequency 86.7, low-frequency 88.3 average AUC. The backbone is FaRL+UniFormerV2, and the paper explicitly motivates it with 'identity inconsistency' (mixture proportions of source and target ID differ across frames). This is already 'temporal SBI with time-varying blend strength', and it already studies the frequency of the variation.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: Self-blending only: no foreign identity is blended in. It works in pixel space on a spatio-temporal ViT, not on face-recognition embedding trajectories. It has no real-only predictive or anomaly objective. Training is contrastive pre-training followed by fine-tuning on FF++ real and fake data, so it is not fake-free at the final stage.

closest_works.title: Unsupervised Multimodal Deepfake Detection Using Intra- and Cross-Modal Inconsistencies
closest_works.exact_overlap: Verified. It is trained only on real VoxCeleb2. Per-frame AdaFace identity features (fine-tuned end-to-end) are pooled by a transformer per time window. An intra-modal contrastive loss makes same-video windows similar and different-identity windows dissimilar. At test time the fake score is the n-th percentile of the T x T identity self-similarity matrix of the video, with no reference video. It gives an information-theoretic argument that identity or motion inconsistency is unavoidable. This is real-only, reference-free anomaly scoring of a face-recognition identity trajectory, which is the core of Idea F(1).
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It uses no forecasting or masked prediction of the next embedding (contrastive self-similarity instead) and no pseudo-fakes. It evaluates only on FakeAVCeleb and KoDF (adversarial subset), not FF++ to CDF/DFD. Identity-only AUC on FakeAVCeleb is only about 77.9, and the authors show it collapses on low-motion videos. It explicitly argues against likelihood or prediction-based scoring (as in AVAD), so a forecasting variant must beat it empirically.

closest_works.title: Self-Supervised Video Forensics by Audio-Visual Anomaly Detection (AVAD)
closest_works.exact_overlap: An autoregressive model trained on real videos only predicts the next-step feature trajectory (audio-visual synchronisation features), and low likelihood (high prediction loss) flags a manipulation. This is exactly the forecasting-as-anomaly mechanism of F(1).
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: Its signal is audio-visual synchronisation, not identity embeddings. It needs audio and has no pseudo-fakes.

closest_works.title: Can a World Model Predict a Deepfake Video? A Consistency Margin Prior for Deepfake Detection (ConsistencyNet)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Verified. It uses V-JEPA 2.1 latent prediction residuals (predictor output vs. frozen encoder target for the future latent positions) as the forensic signal, with a margin prior that the residual is larger for fakes than for reals. Visual-only, latent-space forecasting error as the detection cue. Reports FF++ to CDF 90.5, DFDC 87.1, and DF40 face-swap average 95.5.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: Supervised with FF++ fakes (weighted CE plus margin), not real-only anomaly scoring. It uses generic V-JEPA patch latents, not identity embeddings, and no pseudo-fakes. It still pre-empts any claim of 'first to use self-supervised latent video prediction error for deepfake detection'.

closest_works.title: Beyond Flicker: Detecting Kinematic Inconsistencies for Generalizable Deepfake Video Detection (KiMoI)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Verified. A transformer autoencoder (LPN) learns natural landmark-motion bases from real CelebV-HQ. Per-timestep Gaussian noise on one basis weight breaks natural motion correlations, and the pristine frames are morphed to match, giving temporal pseudo-fakes from real data only. These are mixed with SBI to train MARLIN on pristine data only (CDF 94.7, DFD 97.0, DFDCP 93.9, DF40 average 97.7). It directly compares CBI, VB and noise baselines. This is the 'learn natural dynamics from real video, then synthesise temporal pseudo-fakes' recipe that F proposes.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: Its signal is landmark kinematics, not identity. It does no cross-identity blending and uses no anomaly or prediction-error score; the detector is a pixel ViT classifier.

closest_works.title: Generalizing Video DeepFake Detection by Self-generated Audio-Visual Pseudo-Fakes (AVPF)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Verified. Visual self-blending blends a temporally shifted copy of the face into the original inside a convex-hull mask, using a per-frame blend factor alpha_t in [0,1] built from temporal window masks smoothed with a triangular kernel. Table 4C shows localised time-varying windows beat whole-sequence blending. Real-only training (VoxCeleb2) beats real-only AVH-Align, SpeechForensics and AVAD.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: The source is a time-shifted copy of the same person, not a different identity. It works on the lip ROI with AV-HuBERT, has no identity-embedding modelling, and is not evaluated on FF++ to CDF.

closest_works.title: Vulnerability-Aware Spatio-Temporal Learning for Generalizable Deepfake Video Detection (FakeSTormer, Self-Blended Video)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Video-level self-blended pseudo-fakes; a TimeSformer is trained on FF++ real videos plus SBV only (CDF 92.8, DFD 98.6, DFDCP 90.2). This is the canonical fake-free 'video SBI' baseline.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: SBI parameters are held constant across frames (by design no blend-strength jitter). It does no identity blending and uses no identity features or anomaly scoring. Its method was read via the KiMoI and MoSTE descriptions plus a search snippet, not the full text.

closest_works.title: Generalizing Deepfake Video Detection with Plug-and-Play: Video-Level Blending and Spatiotemporal Adapter Tuning (VB + StA)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Builds real-only video pseudo-fakes by independently warping and self-blending facial organs in each frame (Facial Feature Drift), which injects frame-to-frame jitter.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: The jitter is geometric warping of the same identity, not identity mixing, and there is no identity-embedding detector or anomaly scoring.

closest_works.title: Detecting Deepfake by Creating Spatio-Temporal Regularity Disruption (P-fake generator)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Real-only pseudo-fake videos in which per-frame or run-wise random edit, mask and blend parameters disrupt temporal regularity. An early instance of time-varying blending used for temporal pseudo-fakes.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: No foreign identity and no identity-embedding detector.

closest_works.title: AltFreezing for More General Video Face Forgery Detection (clip-level blending, CBI)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Clip-level blending pastes a face clip, possibly from another video or identity, into a background clip frame by frame. This is cross-identity, video-level pseudo-fake synthesis.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: Blend strength and mask are constant over the clip (no jitter). Training still uses FF++ fakes, and there is no identity-embedding modelling.

closest_works.title: Fake It till You Make It: Curricular Dynamic Forgery Augmentations (SSBI)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Verified. Self-shifted Blending Image blends the face of another frame of the same video (shift of 5-10 frames) to mimic temporal inconsistency. It is one of BI (cross-identity), SBI and SSBI, chosen by a learned policy, and also runs in a real-only setting (Table C2).
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: Frame-level detector; no temporal jitter sequence and no identity trajectory model.

closest_works.title: DiffFake: Exposing Deepfakes using Differential Anomaly Detection
closest_works.exact_overlap: Verified. A GMM anomaly model is fitted only on pairs of real same-video face embeddings (differences such as (A-B)^2) to learn natural changes between frames of one person. The embedding backbone is trained on local and global SBI-style pseudo-fakes. This combines 'real-only modelling of natural face-embedding change' with pseudo-fakes in one detector, conceptually very close to F(1)+(2).
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It uses pairs of frames sampled far apart, not ordered trajectories or forecasting. The embeddings come from an SBI-trained EfficientNet, not identity (ArcFace). There is no temporal jitter synthesis.

closest_works.title: Learning Natural Consistency Representation for Face Forgery Video Detection (NACO)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Self-supervised masked per-frame feature prediction (Spatial Predictive Module) on real VoxCeleb2 videos, plus frame-shuffle negatives. This is masked trajectory modelling learned from real videos.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: Generic CNN features rather than identity embeddings. The final detector is a supervised head fine-tuned on FF++ fakes, not a prediction-error anomaly score.

closest_works.title: Protecting Celebrities from DeepFake with Identity Consistency Transformer (ICT)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Real-only training in which identity-inconsistent pseudo-fakes are made by swapping inner faces between different real identities. This is the 'blend in a different identity' half of F(2).
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: Image-level (inner/outer identity), with no temporal variation of blend strength.

verdicts.strongest_refutation:
Idea F is the union of two components, and each is published nearly verbatim. A reviewer can assemble that union from about four papers.

(2) 'Temporal SBI with time-varying blend strength, using only real videos' is UniForensics' Dynamic Video Self-Blending (arXiv 2407.19079). It samples every SBI parameter per frame and low-pass filters the sequence in the DCT domain so blend strength drifts smoothly. It motivates this with source/target identity proportions that 'differ across frames', and its Table V already ablates static vs. white-noise vs. high, mid and low-frequency jitter. AVPF (2604.09110) uses an explicit per-frame alpha_t in [0,1] (windowed, triangular-smoothed) on real-only data and shows localised temporal blending beats whole-clip blending. P-fake/STC (2207.10402) and VB (CVPR'25) inject per-frame parameter jitter. FakeSTormer's SBV (ICCV'25) sets the fake-free video SOTA. Blending in a *different* identity is covered at video level by AltFreezing's CBI (cross-clip, CVPR'23), at frame level by BI/ICT, and by SSBI's cross-frame blending (ECCV'24). 'Cross-identity + time-varying alpha' is therefore a one-line recombination of DVSB with CBI/BI.

(1) 'Real-only identity-trajectory anomaly detection' is Tian et al. (2311.17088). It trains AdaFace identity features plus a temporal transformer on real VoxCeleb2 only and scores a video by its own T x T identity self-similarity, reference-free. Swapping that contrastive score for a next/masked-embedding forecasting error is exactly AVAD (CVPR'23, autoregressive prediction error on a per-frame feature trajectory, real-only). Latent prediction residuals for visual deepfake detection were also just published in ConsistencyNet (V-JEPA 2.1, 2611.21846, Nov 2026). Masked per-frame feature prediction on real videos is NACO (ECCV'24). DiffFake (2502.16247) already fits a real-only anomaly model on face-embedding changes between frames of the same person and pairs it with SBI-style pseudo-fakes, which is the combined (1)+(2) philosophy without the temporal ordering. KiMoI (2512.04175) already 'learns natural facial dynamics from real video and perturbs them to synthesise temporal pseudo-fakes', and it targets reenactment, TI2Net's documented weakness.

A harsh AC would summarise Idea F as 'Tian et al. + AVAD-style forecasting + DVSB/CBI with ArcFace instead of pixels'. Moreover, Tian et al.'s own analysis (identity-only AUC of about 78 on FakeAVCeleb, near useless on low-motion videos) predicts that an identity-only detector will remain weak on reenactment no matter how it is trained. Identity-jitter pseudo-fakes by construction do not simulate reenactment, where identity is preserved.
verdicts.remaining_novel_delta:
After reading the method sections, I found no paper that does all of the following together. (a) Defines and calibrates temporal pseudo-fakes in face-recognition identity space. Concretely: blend a *different* identity (or an identity-perturbed self-swap) into real video with a time-varying alpha_t, then measure and control the resulting ArcFace-trajectory jitter (amplitude, spectrum, burstiness), for example by matching the identity-jitter spectrum measured on real deepfakes (FF++/CDF/DF40). DVSB filters pixel-blend parameters but never measures the induced identity signal. CBI is cross-identity but constant over time. (b) Uses those pseudo-fakes to train or regularise a lightweight, frozen-face-recognition-embedding trajectory model (TI2Net-class, about 1M parameters) rather than a pixel ViT. (c) Combines a real-only next/masked-identity forecasting prior with pseudo-fake supervision and evaluates it on the standard FF++ to DFD/DFo/CDF/DF40 protocol. Tian et al. never evaluated there, and no identity-trajectory method has been trained fake-free there.

A possibly cheaper variant is also unpublished as far as I found: synthesising jitter directly in embedding space (perturbing ArcFace trajectories without rendering). It is a weak contribution, though, because reviewers will flag shortcut learning. So the delta is (i) an identity-space measurement and calibration of temporal pseudo-fakes and (ii) a fake-free, identity-trajectory detector benchmarked against the pixel pseudo-fake family. It is an incremental recombination, not a new paradigm. Its value depends on empirical results: beating TI2Net's CDF2 68.2 is not enough. It must be competitive with, or clearly complementary to, FakeSTormer, KiMoI, VB and DVSB, and it must be honest about reenactment.
verdicts.recommended_reframing:
Do not pitch this as 'temporal SBI' or 'first real-only identity-dynamics detector'. Both claims are refuted: 'Temporal SBI' is also already the name used by 2610.11706, DVSB has time-varying blending, and Tian et al. 2023 is real-only identity anomaly detection.

Pitch it as 'Identity-calibrated temporal pseudo-fakes for fake-free identity-trajectory forensics'. The contributions would be:
(1) An analysis that measures the identity-jitter signature (spectrum and amplitude of ArcFace/AdaFace trajectory deviations, conditioned on pose) of real face-swap deepfakes vs. real videos vs. existing video pseudo-fakes (DVSB, SBV, VB, CBI, KiMoI). This shows that pixel-space pseudo-fakes produce mismatched identity dynamics.
(2) A cross-identity, time-varying blending generator whose alpha_t is chosen to match that measured identity signature: identity-matched donors, pose-matched as in BI, with spectrum-matched alpha_t.
(3) A small identity-trajectory model trained fake-free, with a forecasting or masked-identity pretext on real data plus pseudo-fake supervision. Pose and expression conditioning must be included, because pose-induced ArcFace drift otherwise dominates the prediction error on real videos.
(4) Positioning as a cheap, interpretable, plug-in complement: show that its score fuses with pixel detectors (FakeSTormer/KiMoI) for gains on face-swap.

State explicitly that identity jitter does not cover reenactment. Either pair it with a motion or kinematic branch or report the limitation; F2F and DF40-reenactment numbers must be shown.

Required experiments:
- The same identity-trajectory detector trained with each pseudo-fake generator: DVSB, SBV, VB, CBI, SSBI, KiMoI, and yours.
- Scoring ablations: forecasting error vs. Tian et al.'s self-similarity percentile vs. a DiffFake-style GMM.
- Ablation over the alpha_t spectrum, mirroring DVSB Table V but measured in identity space.

verdicts.name: Region-level identity trajectories

closest_works.title: MOTIF: Person-of-Interest Deepfake Detection Beyond 3DMM Coefficients
closest_works.exact_overlap: Read in full. Per frame it fits 3DDFA-V3 and builds a 150-d vector (80 shape, 64 expression, 3 pose, 3 translation). A 12-block temporal transformer encodes 75-frame windows, trained with multi-depth NT-Xent identity-contrastive loss on VoxCeleb2 real videos only. A separate part-level branch encodes the 968 reconstructed lip vertices (temporal mean removed) with its own temporal transformer. Scores are fused after per-POI z-calibration. The factorial ablation finds that dynamic shape alone gives 90.4 vs 90.6 for the full vector, and the dynamic reading helps most on reenactment. The mouth branch adds +9.1 AUC on FakeAVCeleb lip-sync and +3.6 on KoDF reenactment. Evaluation covers face swap, reenactment (FOMM, LivePortrait, HelloMeme, Memo) and lip-sync (Wav2Lip, Diff2Lip, LatentSync). In short, it already does '3DMM shape trajectories + a part-level 3D trajectory, fused, aimed at reenactment and lip-sync'.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It is reference-based (POI enrollment with leave-one-out calibration), not a reference-free binary detector trained on FF++. The only region is the mouth, and the conclusion explicitly says 'facial regions other than the mouth remain to be explored'. It has no per-region appearance identity embeddings (ArcFace-style), no first-order differencing, no GRU or triplet loss, and no cross-region consistency term. It also notes that per-frame shape coefficients absorb expression, and suggests a clip-consistent 3DMM fit as future work.

closest_works.title: Mining Temporal Inconsistency with 3D Face Model for Deepfake Video Detection
closest_works.exact_overlap: A reference-free, supervised deepfake video detector. Per frame it fits a 3D face model and uses the 2D-landmark vs 3D-reprojection distance plus 3D shape and texture features. An RNN models them over time, and the paper reports strong cross-manipulation results. This is the '3DMM shape trajectory + RNN, reference-free' half of Idea D.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: The face is treated globally, with no part-level shape or identity and no per-region identity embeddings. It is framed around face swapping rather than reenactment or lip-sync. Only the abstract was read.

closest_works.title: Face Forgery Detection Based on Facial Region Displacement Trajectory Series (FTDN)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Tracks multiple facial ROIs over 64 frames and models them jointly with spatial-temporal graph attention plus a GRU. Reports its largest gains on Face2Face and NeuralTextures (reenactment), which is the 'multiple regions x time, joint model, catches reenactment' structure of Idea D.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: The per-region signal is geometric displacement (optical-flow anchors), not identity embeddings or 3DMM shape. It has no identity framing.

closest_works.title: Forged facial video detection framework based on multi-region temporal relationship feature
closest_works.exact_overlap: Extracts local features of multiple facial regions with 3D attention, then models how the relationships between regions evolve over time with a time-series graph CNN. It detects forgery from the temporal inconsistency of those inter-region relationships, which is the 'joint regional temporal inconsistency' mechanism.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: The regional features are generic appearance features, not identity or 3DMM shape. There is no reenactment or lip-sync framing and no identity motivation.

closest_works.title: Protecting Celebrities from DeepFake with Identity Consistency Transformer (ICT)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Region-level identity: separate inner-face and outer-face identity vectors with a consistency loss. This is the canonical 'local identity inconsistency' precedent.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It is frame-level with no temporal trajectories. Inner and outer regions are its only parts. It targets swaps, and reenactment and lip-sync keep both regions' identity.

closest_works.title: RAIRNet: Region-Aware Identity Rectification for Face Forgery Detection
closest_works.exact_overlap: Argues explicitly that forged identity is hybrid and regionally distributed, so a single global ID vector misses local inconsistency. It uses region-aware identity filters with local/global weighting. This is the core premise of Idea D.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: Image-level only, with no temporal trajectories and no 3DMM. Its regions come from learned filters rather than semantic parts.

closest_works.title: Face2Parts: Exploring Coarse-to-Fine Inter-Regional Facial Dependencies for Generalized Deepfake Detection
closest_works.exact_overlap: Read. It crops frame, face, left eye, right eye, lips and nose with Dlib, encodes each part separately (CLIP ViT, or MViT/TVC/ViViT for clips), and models inter-region dependencies with channel attention plus triplet learning. Training is FF++ with cross-dataset tests on CDF, DFD, DFDC and PDD (lip-sync), and it reports gains on F2F/NT. This is the 'per-part embeddings + triplet loss + FF++ protocol' combination.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: The per-part features are CLIP or video-backbone appearance features, not identity. There is no explicit per-part temporal trajectory or differencing (temporal backbones only pool clips), and no 3DMM.

closest_works.title: Ariadne's Thread of LipSync: Unraveling Forgeries via Inconsistency between Lip Motions and Head Poses (LipDA)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Read. It detects lip-sync from the temporal inconsistency between a local region (a lip-ROI ResNet over T-frame windows) and global head-pose landmark trajectories. A margin contrastive loss aligns them for real videos and separates them for fakes. Reports 91.9 AUC cross-manipulation on CelebDF. This is 'local-vs-global temporal inconsistency to catch identity-preserving lip-sync'.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: No identity embeddings or 3DMM shape. It covers the mouth only and is lip-sync specific.

closest_works.title: Improving the Efficiency and Robustness of Deepfakes Detection through Precise Geometric Features (LRNet)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Two-stream GRU over calibrated landmark sequences (eyes, nose, mouth, contour) and their first-order frame differences. This is the same 'parts + differencing + GRU' temporal design as a part-level TI2Net, but on geometry.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: No identity embeddings or 3DMM shape.

closest_works.title: Exploring Static-Dynamic ID Matching and Temporal Static ID Inconsistency for Generalizable Deepfake Detection
closest_works.exact_overlap: A reference-free identity-based video detector built specifically to fix TI2Net-style weakness on reenactment. It adds a behaviour (dynamic) ID branch to a temporal static-ID branch, which is the same motivation and protocol as Idea D.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It uses global face identity plus behaviour ID, with no part-level identity or 3DMM shape. Only the abstract was read.

closest_works.title: Within 3DMM Space: Exploring Inherent 3D Artifact for Video Forgery Detection (3DAD)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Reference-free spatio-temporal inconsistency modelled in 3DMM semantic space, using a 3D analysis unit pre-trained on 3DMM reconstruction plus a texture unit.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: The face is global, with no per-part identity and no identity framing.

closest_works.title: Robust Deepfake Detection for Electronic Know Your Customer Systems Using Registered Images
closest_works.exact_overlap: A direct TI2Net upgrade that keeps temporal identity differences and targets reenactment. Its ablation confirms that global temporal identity alone fails on reenactment.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It fixes reenactment with a registered reference image, not with part-level identity or shape.

verdicts.strongest_refutation: A harsh area chair would say that Idea D is a recombination of published components, with no new mechanism. (1) The 3DMM half is already published twice. Reference-free, per-frame 3D shape and texture trajectories with an RNN appear in Cheng et al., PRCV 2023. Shape-coefficient trajectories plus a separate part-level (mouth) 3D trajectory, fused and explicitly aimed at reenactment and lip-sync, appear in MOTIF (arXiv 2610.09830, Oct 2026). MOTIF's own ablation already shows that dynamic shape carries almost all the signal and helps most on reenactment, and that a part-level mouth trajectory adds +9.1 AUC on lip-sync. (2) The 'joint multi-region temporal' half is published as geometric ROI trajectories with graph attention and a GRU (FTDN, WACV-W 2023), largest gains on F2F/NT. It is also published as inter-region relationship dynamics (Fang et al., AIP Advances 2023), landmark-part GRU with differences (LRNet, CVPR 2021), and component-guided CLIP temporal modelling (FCG, 2404.05583, plus its 2026 landmark-guided extension). (3) The 'local identity beats global identity' premise is ICT (CVPR 2022, inner vs outer) and RAIRNet (MM 2023, region-aware identity). Per-part embeddings with triplet learning under the FF++ cross-dataset protocol is Face2Parts (2026). (4) The 'local vs global temporal inconsistency catches lip-sync' insight is LipDA (ICML 2026), plus the LIPINC line. (5) Replacing the global ID with something that survives reenactment, reference-free, is the IET Biometrics 2024 static/dynamic-ID paper. The only remaining combination is 'per-part identity embeddings over time, reference-free'. There is also a technical objection to that combination. Reenactment and lip-sync generators preserve the target's appearance in each region (the mouth is re-rendered from the target's own texture). So per-region appearance identity is near-constant by construction, and any signal that remains is shape or motion, which MOTIF, LRNet, FTDN and LipDA already capture. Face recognition networks are also not trained to give stable identity from eye, nose or mouth crops, so part 'identity' embeddings will be dominated by expression and pose. MOTIF itself documents that per-frame 3DMM shape absorbs expression. A reviewer would ask why this is not just MOTIF made reference-free plus LRNet with different features.
verdicts.remaining_novel_delta: Narrow, but real if it is executed and argued carefully. (a) No paper I found computes identity embeddings per facial part (e.g., periocular, nose and mouth recognition encoders, or a face-recognition model with region masking) and models their trajectories over time. Every region-temporal method uses geometry, landmarks, optical flow, CLIP or appearance features. Every identity-temporal method (TI2Net, It Wasn't Me, eKYC, PIA, Facial Biometric Anomalies, IET 2024) uses one global face embedding. (b) No paper models identity consistency jointly over time and across regions, in a reference-free, FF++-trained binary setting. By that I mean a regions x time identity tensor whose cross-region agreement is tested, e.g., whether eye-region identity drifts in step with mouth-region identity. MOTIF is reference-based, covers the mouth only, and leaves 'other regions' and 'a clip-consistent 3DMM fit' as future work. (c) An expression-disentangled per-region 3D shape trajectory is unclaimed: fit one clip-level shape and track per-region residual shape after removing the expression basis. This directly answers MOTIF's stated limitation that per-frame shape absorbs expression, and Cheng 2023 and 3DAD do not do it. (d) A reference-free counterpart of MOTIF's part branch, trained on FF++ and evaluated under the TI2Net protocol (DFD, DFo, CDF1/2) plus reenactment and lip-sync sets, is open as an empirical contribution. Each of these is incremental, and (a) carries the technical risk described in the refutation.
verdicts.recommended_reframing: Do not pitch 'region-level identity trajectories' as a new idea. Pitch it as a fix for a measured failure of temporal identity detectors. Proposed framing: 'Identity should be invariant along two axes, time and facial part. Reenactment and lip-sync break the part axis while preserving the global one.' Concretely: (1) Build a reference-free spatio-temporal identity consistency tensor, regions x time, from part-masked face-recognition embeddings (or part-specific recognition encoders such as periocular). Pair it with a clip-consistent 3DMM fit that gives one identity shape per clip and per-region residual shape after projecting out expression. This is presented as the explicit fix for the shape/expression leakage MOTIF reports. (2) Model two kinds of inconsistency: per-part temporal differences (TI2Net-style), and cross-part identity agreement over time (a new loss or score). (3) The key experiment: show that global ArcFace differences (TI2Net), landmark trajectories (LRNet, FTDN), and MOTIF-style mouth geometry made reference-free each fail on a specific subset that the part-identity tensor catches. Candidate subsets are F2F/NT trained on DF, FOMM/LivePortrait, and Wav2Lip/LatentSync. Then show that the part-identity signal is not just expression leakage, for example by controlling for expression with AU or 3DMM-expression regressors. Without (3) the paper reads as LRNet + ICT + MOTIF combined. Also report results under the TI2Net protocol for direct comparison, and on DeepSpeak/KoDF/FakeAVCeleb for reenactment and lip-sync.

verdicts.name: Cross-modal voice-face identity consistency over time

closest_works.title: Spotting Audio-Visual Inconsistencies (SAVI) in Manipulated Video (Bolles et al., SRI / UvA)
closest_works.exact_overlap: This is the core logic of Idea I, published nine years ago, and the sweep missed it. Read in full. It tracks speaker identity within one video separately in each modality: i-vector/PLDA speaker diarization on 2 s audio blocks, and a CNN face-ID per face tracklet. For every pair of time segments it estimates P(same speaker | audio) and P(same face | video), then flags tampering when 'the voice of this talking face changed during the video, but not the face itself, or vice versa' (Eq. 3). It is explicitly reference-free ('without knowing the actual identity'). In effect it compares the audio identity self-similarity structure over time with the visual one, which is 'audio and face identity trajectories disagree'.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It predates deepfakes. It targets splicing (identity changes at shot cuts, AMI meeting data) with i-vectors, hand-built probabilities and no learning on fakes. It does not use first-order identity drift, does not model fine-grained within-shot jitter, uses no modern embeddings (ECAPA, WavLM, ArcFace) and has no learned temporal model. It is not evaluated on any deepfake benchmark.

closest_works.title: Synthetic Speech Detection Based on Temporal Consistency and Distribution of Speaker Features (Zhang et al.)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Read in full. This is literally TI2Net applied to voice. It extracts ECAPA-TDNN speaker features (multi-layer feature aggregation) over time, takes consecutive differences d_i = s_{i+1} - s_i, and feeds them to a 2-layer GRU (last hidden state) and a classifier. It cites TI2Net as inspiration, and it shows that TTS voices are too temporally consistent while VC voices drift. So the 'voice identity trajectory and its drift' half of Idea I is already published with the exact TI2Net recipe.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: Audio only. There is no face stream and no cross-modal comparison of voice drift with face drift. It is evaluated on ASVspoof and In-the-Wild, not on audio-visual deepfakes.

closest_works.title: Voice-Face Homogeneity Tells Deepfake (VFD) (Cheng et al.)
closest_works.venue_year: ACM TOMM 2023 (arXiv v2 withdrawn for 'incorrect experiment setting'; v3 current)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Read the v3 method. It detects deepfakes by voice-face identity mismatch: transformer face and voice identity extractors, pre-trained on VoxCeleb2 with identity cross-entropy plus InfoNCE in a joint voice-face space, then fine-tuned with a real-fake contrastive loss. At test time, cosine voice-face similarity below a threshold means fake. It claims to be the first to do this.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It is static: one random face frame against one 3 s voice clip. There are no windows, no trajectories and no drift. The authors state it fails when both voice and face are edited to the same target identity, which is the case a trajectory-based method might address.

closest_works.title: Unsupervised Multimodal Deepfake Detection Using Intra- and Cross-Modal Inconsistencies (Tian et al.)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Read in full. It is reference-free and trained only on real VoxCeleb2. It splits a video into T windows. Per-window AdaFace + transformer identity vectors give a T x T intra-modal identity self-similarity matrix (an identity trajectory and its consistency). A per-window visual vs Whisper-audio contrastive branch gives a cross-modal score, and the two scores are summed. It reports 96.8 AUC on FakeAVCeleb and also tests on KoDF. It also explains when identity drift appears via an identity-motion trade-off.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: The audio branch encodes speech content and synchrony (Whisper features aligned to the same window), not speaker identity. It never builds a voice-identity trajectory and never compares voice-identity drift with face-identity drift. There are no first-order differences and the score is a percentile.

closest_works.title: Audio-Visual Person-of-Interest DeepFake Detection (POI-Forensics) (Cozzolino et al.)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Read in full. Per 3 s segment it computes audio-identity and video-identity embeddings (two ResNet-50s trained contrastively on VoxCeleb2 identities, real data only). The segment-wise similarities are aggregated over time for detection. It reports that facial reenactment is the hard case, with AUC about 70-80% (Fig. 5).
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: Each modality is compared with an external reference set of the same person (about 10 videos), not with the other modality in the same video. The audio and video embedding spaces are not aligned, since S_av is the sum of the single-modality scores. There is no drift modelling.

closest_works.title: Referee: Reference-aware Audiovisual Deepfake Detection (Boo, Lee, Lee)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Read in full. It states that 'cross-modal biometric cues ... verifying the correspondence between the speaker's voice and facial appearance' are the detection basis. An identity bottleneck with learnable queries runs over 8 Synchformer audio-visual segments, followed by an ID-matching loss and an AV-Transformer. It reports a cross-dataset AUC of 79.8 on FF++ (audio subset) and 99.4 on KoDF.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: It needs a one-shot reference clip. Voice and face identity are fused into joint tokens, never kept as two separate trajectories. It has no explicit drift or first-order difference modelling.

closest_works.title: PIA: Deepfake Detection Using Phoneme-Temporal and Identity-Dynamic Analysis (Datta et al.)
closest_works.exact_overlap: An audio-visual detector with ArcFace embeddings per frame and an ArcFace temporal-consistency loss on 1 - cos(a_t, a_{t+1}), i.e. face-identity drift inside an audio-visual model.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: Audio enters only as phonemes and visemes. It has no speaker-identity embeddings and no voice-vs-face identity comparison.

closest_works.title: Detecting Deepfake Talking Heads from Facial Biometric Anomalies (Norman & Farid)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Read. It is reference-free and uses the distribution of the all-pairs ArcFace similarity matrix over long talking-head videos (DeepSpeak) to detect face-swap and lip-sync deepfakes. It is motivated by voice-cloning impersonations.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: Face only. Voice identity is not used.

closest_works.title: Identity-Driven Multimedia Forgery Detection via Reference Assistance (IDForge / R-MFDN)
closest_works.exact_overlap: Identity-aware visual and audio features, plus a cross-modal contrastive consistency loss, for detecting face-swap and voice-clone forgeries. Not re-read in detail here; this description comes from the sweep summary and search snippets.
closest_works.what_it_does_not_do: Reference-set based and clip-level. It has no per-window voice-vs-face identity trajectories.

verdicts.strongest_refutation:
Every building block of Idea I is already published, and the composition was partly done in 2017.
(a) Reference-free comparison of how speaker identity evolves over time in audio versus video: Bolles et al., SAVI, CVPRW 2017. Per-segment audio speaker identity (i-vector/PLDA) and per-tracklet face-ID are compared pairwise across time. A video is flagged when the voice identity changes but the face does not, or vice versa. This is 'audio and face identity trajectories disagree' within one video, with no reference.
(b) The voice-identity drift branch with exactly TI2Net's recipe (ECAPA features, consecutive differences, GRU last state, classifier): Zhang et al., arXiv 2309.16954 / IEEE SPL, which cites TI2Net.
(c) The face-identity drift branch: TI2Net itself, plus It Wasn't Me (ICIP 2023), Tian et al. 2311.17088 (per-window identity self-similarity), PIA (ICCV-W 2025) and Norman & Farid 2507.08917.
(d) Voice-face identity mismatch as a deepfake cue: VFD (TOMM 2023), POI-Forensics (CVPRW 2023) and Referee (2025/26, which frames detection explicitly as voice-face biometric correspondence).
(e) Reference-free, per-window, real-only identity trajectory plus a per-window audio-visual check in one score: Tian et al. 2311.17088.
A harsh area chair would therefore say the proposal is SAVI's identity-change consistency test re-implemented with modern embeddings: two published TI2Net-style drift encoders (TI2Net and 2309.16954) plus a cross-modal fusion head, all already motivated by VFD, POI-Forensics and Referee. That is an incremental combination.
There is also a substantive technical objection. Idea I is pitched as a TI2Net upgrade, but it does not fix TI2Net's documented weakness. In face reenactment (Face2Face, NeuralTextures), audio-driven lip-sync (Wav2Lip) and talking-head avatars, the face identity is the target's, and the voice is usually the target's real voice or a clone of it. Neither the static voice-face match nor the identity trajectories need to disagree. POI-Forensics and Tian et al. both report reenactment as their hardest case.
Finally, TI2Net's own benchmarks (FF++ to Celeb-DF/DFD/DeeperForensics) mostly do not carry meaningful manipulated audio. In FF++ face swaps the original target audio is kept, so the static voice-face mismatch already catches them. The idea therefore cannot be evaluated on TI2Net's protocol and has to move to FakeAVCeleb, AV-Deepfake1M(++), KoDF, DeepSpeak or IDForge, where VFD, Tian et al., Referee and AVFF-class detectors are already at 95-99 AUC.
verdicts.remaining_novel_delta:
A narrow delta remains. As far as the searches show (through Nov 2026), no published work learns, end to end and without a reference, the joint dynamics of two separate identity trajectories within one video: a speaker-embedding drift sequence (ECAPA/WavLM, consecutive differences) and a face-identity drift sequence (ArcFace/AdaFace, consecutive differences). None classifies fakes from their differential behaviour, for example cross-modal correlation of drift, lagged co-variation, or one modality too stable while the other jitters. SAVI does this only at the coarse level of discrete speaker changes, with hand-built probabilities on spliced meeting videos. 2309.16954 does voice drift only. Tian et al. does face drift plus audio-visual synchrony but not voice identity. VFD, POI-Forensics and Referee are static or reference-based.
The plausibly new and testable claim is the one VFD lists as its own failure case. When both voice and face are synthesized toward the same target identity (FakeAVCeleb FVFA, AV-Deepfake1M++, DeepSpeak v2 voice-clone plus face-swap), the static voice-face match succeeds. However, the dynamics may still differ: TTS/VC voice embeddings are anomalously stable (per 2309.16954) while face-swap identity jitters, or the reverse. Real videos show coupled natural variation, from shared factors such as emotion, effort and head-microphone geometry. That 'drift-coupling' hypothesis is the only defensible novelty, and it is unverified. If real voice and face identity drift turn out not to co-vary (very likely: speaker embeddings vary with phonetic content, face embeddings with pose), the signal reduces to two independent unimodal drift detectors plus late fusion, which is not novel.
verdicts.recommended_reframing:
Do not sell this as 'temporal cross-modal identity consistency' or as the first voice-face identity deepfake detector. SAVI (2017), VFD (2022/23), POI-Forensics (2023) and Referee (2025) together kill that claim.
Reframe it narrowly as a reference-free test of whether the two identity streams co-evolve, targeting same-identity multimodal forgeries where static voice-face matching fails. Concretely:
(1) State the hypothesis as a measurable property of real data. Real voice-identity drift and face-identity drift share structure, for example coupling after controlling for phonetic content and head pose, while TTS/VC and face swap break that coupling. Verify it first on VoxCeleb2/LRS3 with ECAPA and ArcFace before building any model. If no coupling exists in real data, drop the idea.
(2) Position the model as a generalisation of SAVI's change-consistency test (continuous drift instead of discrete speaker changes) and of 2309.16954 plus TI2Net (two drift encoders with a learned cross-drift interaction, such as cross-attention or a cross-modal drift self-similarity matrix, rather than late fusion).
(3) Train on real data only, as Tian et al. and POI-Forensics do, or report both settings.
(4) Evaluate where audio is meaningful: FakeAVCeleb (especially FVFA and RVFA), AV-Deepfake1M++, KoDF, DeepSpeak v2 and IDForge. Include a stratified analysis of same-identity forgeries (voice-clone plus face-swap to the same target) where VFD-style static matching fails. Report honestly that the method does not address FF++ reenactment.
(5) Ablations must show that the cross-drift term adds over (a) the static voice-face similarity (VFD-style), (b) the face-only drift encoder (TI2Net), (c) the voice-only drift encoder (2309.16954) and (d) their late fusion.
In a TI2Net-upgrade paper, this is better as a secondary component or extension section than as the headline contribution.

A.title: Critical Contour Prior-Guided Graph Learning With Pose Calibration for Identity-Aware Deepfake Detection (CP-GAT)
A.authors: Liyue Ming, Peisong He, Haoliang Li, Shiqi Wang, Xinghao Jiang
A.what_it_does: Identity-aware, reference-based deepfake detector. Its stated motivation is that head pose degrades identity-consistency methods. It builds a graph over contour landmarks and adds a rotation-compensation block trained with 'pose-calibrated contrastive learning', which pulls features toward high-quality frontal faces. Detection is the similarity between the identity features of the query and of reference samples.
A.overlap_explanation: This is the closest deepfake paper on the nuisance side. It has the same goal of stopping head pose from contaminating the identity signal used for forgery detection. The mechanism differs: it learns pose-invariant (frontal-calibrated) identity features and compares them against references. It does not learn from real videos a model of how much the embedding should change for a given pose or expression change, and it does not score the unexplained residual over time. It is also reference-based, whereas TI2Net is reference-free. Cite it as the main 'pose-robust identity forensics' prior and compare against it.

A.title: Unmasking Puppeteers: Leveraging Biometric Leakage to Expose Impersonation in AI-based Videoconferencing
A.authors: Danial Samadi Vahdati, Tai Duc Nguyen, Koki Nagano, David Luebke, Orazio Gallo, Ekta Prashnani, Matthew Stamm
A.what_it_does: Detects puppeteering in talking-head video calls from the pose-expression latents. A pose-conditioned large-margin contrastive loss uses pose-matched negatives (a different identity rendered at the same pose) so that pose and expression are cancelled and identity cues are amplified. An LSTM fuses per-frame similarity to the reference. Frames with extreme yaw are filtered out, and this filtering measurably improves AUC.
A.overlap_explanation: It shares the core concern that pose and expression variance swamp the identity signal, and it removes that variance explicitly with conditioning on pose. The removal is done by contrastive invariance learning, not by regressing the expected embedding change and keeping the residual. The setting also differs: the signal is the codec latent (not ArcFace on RGB), the task is puppeteering (not real-vs-fake), and a reference portrait is required. Its pose-matched hard-negative idea and its yaw-filtering ablation transfer directly to Idea A.

A.title: Exploring Static–Dynamic ID Matching and Temporal Static ID Inconsistency for Generalizable Deepfake Detection
A.authors: Huimin She, Yongjian Hu, Beibei Liu, Chang-Tsun Li
A.what_it_does: Reference-free, manipulation-independent detector with two branches. One checks temporal anomalies of the image-level static ID (a face-recognition embedding), as TI2Net does. The other checks whether the clip-level static ID (appearance) and the clip-level dynamic ID (facial behavior) match. It adds a static-dynamic ID matching loss and a dynamic ID constraint loss, and claims to detect both face swapping and reenactment.
A.overlap_explanation: It combines TI2Net-style temporal identity inconsistency with a behaviour/motion stream and targets the same weakness (reenactment) without references. It does not model identity drift conditioned on nuisance changes. Behaviour is treated as a second identity cue that must match, not as an explanatory variable whose effect is subtracted. It is a direct competitor that must be compared against, especially on Face2Face/NeuralTextures.

A.title: Robust Deepfake Detection for Electronic Know Your Customer Systems Using Registered Images
A.authors: Takuma Amada, Kazuya Kakizaki, Taiki Miyagawa, Akinori F. Ebihara, Kaede Shiohara, Toshihiko Yamasaki
A.what_it_does: A direct TI2Net extension. It keeps TI2Net's temporal differences (TDC), adds differences to a registered image (ADC), and uses the same CE + triplet + anchor-positive losses with an RNN. Swapping ArcFace (MS1MV2) for AdaFace (quality-adaptive margin, WebFace12M) raises cross-dataset AUC sharply (CDF 50.8 to 75.9 when trained on KoDF). It also shows that random frame sampling generalizes better than sliding windows.
A.overlap_explanation: It shares the TI2Net base and the 'quality-aware face embedding' component: AdaFace's quality-adaptive training is what reduces quality-induced false variation. It does not explicitly estimate or regress out quality, pose or expression. This is a critical confound baseline. Idea A must show gains beyond simply using AdaFace or WebFace12M embeddings in TI2Net.

A.title: It Wasn't Me: Irregular Identity in Deepfake Videos
A.authors: Honggu Liu, Paolo Bestagini, Lin Huang, Wenbo Zhou, Stefano Tubaro, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu
A.what_it_does: Trains a classifier on time series of facial identity features, because frame-by-frame generators make identity less temporally stable. It claims robustness on low-quality video and promising cross-dataset results.
A.overlap_explanation: This is the same base signal as TI2Net (temporal instability of FR identity features), published concurrently. It has no nuisance conditioning or residual modelling, so it shares only the base component. It is a necessary related-work and baseline citation.

A.title: PIA: Deepfake Detection Using Phoneme-Temporal and Identity-Dynamic Analysis
A.authors: Soumyya Kanti Datta, Tanvi Ranga, Chengzhe Sun, Siwei Lyu
A.what_it_does: Audio-visual detector with a stream of per-frame ArcFace identity embeddings ('ArcFace drift'). It adds an ArcFace temporal consistency loss that penalizes 1 - cos(a_t, a_{t+1}) between consecutive frames, alongside phoneme/viseme and lip-geometry streams.
A.overlap_explanation: It uses raw consecutive ArcFace drift as a forensic cue, like TI2Net. It does not account for pose, expression or quality causing the drift. It is evidence that raw identity drift is in active use, and so motivates the 'explained vs unexplained drift' distinction.

A.title: ID-Reveal: Identity-aware DeepFake Video Detection
A.authors: Davide Cozzolino, Andreas Rössler, Justus Thies, Matthias Nießner, Luisa Verdoliva
A.what_it_does: Extracts per-frame 3DMM coefficients (expression and pose), learns a temporal embedding of how a person moves using metric learning on real videos only (plus an adversarial branch), and detects fakes by distance to reference videos of the same person. It generalizes well to reenactment.
A.overlap_explanation: It shares the per-frame 3DMM nuisance estimation and training on real videos only. In ID-Reveal, however, the 3DMM dynamics are the identity signal (behavioural biometrics), not nuisance factors used to explain away appearance-embedding drift. It also needs reference videos. Idea A inverts its use of 3DMM.

A.title: MOTIF: Person-of-Interest Deepfake Detection Beyond 3DMM Coefficients
A.authors: Giovanni Affatato, Sara Mandelli, Paolo Bestagini, Stefano Tubaro
A.what_it_does: A controlled dissection of 3DMM (3DDFA-V3) coefficient groups for reference-based POI detection, using a temporal transformer trained with NT-Xent on VoxCeleb2. It finds that the shape, expression and pose groups are largely redundant. Per-frame shape coefficients absorb expression dynamics, because a single frame cannot separate shape from expression. Dense mouth vertices add complementary signal. It beats ID-Reveal and POI-Forensics.
A.overlap_explanation: It shares the 3DMM-per-frame front end. Its finding is a direct risk for Idea A: per-frame 3DMM expression and pose estimates are entangled with identity, so a nuisance-to-embedding predictor may partly 'explain away' real identity change. Idea A needs a clip-consistent 3DMM fit or a decorrelation check. It does not do residual identity modelling.

A.title: Detecting Deep-Fake Videos from Appearance and Behavior
A.authors: Shruti Agarwal, Hany Farid, Tarek El-Gaaly
A.what_it_does: Combines a static biometric (a face-recognition embedding) with a temporal behavioural biometric (expression and head movement, learned with metric learning). A video is flagged when the appearance identity and the behavioural identity disagree.
A.overlap_explanation: It pairs an FR identity embedding with a pose/expression behavioural model, as Idea A does. The two are compared as two identity estimates, not used to predict embedding change from nuisance change. It is reference/POI-based and aimed at face swaps.

A.title: Audio-Visual Person-of-Interest DeepFake Detection (POI-Forensics)
A.authors: Davide Cozzolino, Alessandro Pianese, Matthias Nießner, Luisa Verdoliva
A.what_it_does: Learns audio and visual identity embeddings with contrastive learning on real videos, so that segments of the same identity are close. A test video is compared against the POI's reference set, which makes it a manipulation-agnostic detector.
A.overlap_explanation: Identity-consistency forensics trained on real data only. It has no nuisance-conditioned residual, needs references, and the signal is multimodal. It is related context only.

A.title: Pose-Robust Face Recognition via Deep Residual Equivariant Mapping (DREAM)
A.authors: Kaidi Cao, Yu Rong, Cheng Li, Xiaoou Tang, Chen Change Loy
A.what_it_does: A lightweight block in face-recognition feature space. It adds a learned residual, gated by estimated yaw, that maps a profile face's deep feature toward its frontal-equivalent feature. This explicitly models how an identity embedding shifts as a function of pose.
A.overlap_explanation: From an adjacent field (face recognition), and directly transplantable: it learns embedding shift as a function of a nuisance (yaw), which is the 'expected change' half of Idea A. It is used for canonicalization in recognition, not for temporal residual scoring or forensics. Reviewers may see Idea A's predictor as 'DREAM-style equivariant mapping applied over time', so cite it and position against it.

A.title: Dealing with Uncertainty in Contextual Anomaly Detection
A.authors: Luca Bindini, Lorenzo Perini
A.what_it_does: Contextual anomaly detection. A heteroscedastic Gaussian process regresses behavioural attributes on contextual (environmental) attributes. The anomaly score is a Z-score of the residual, with uncertainty intervals that capture how reliable the assessment is.
A.overlap_explanation: From an adjacent field (anomaly detection), this is the generic form of Idea A's core mechanism: predict the indicator variable (identity-embedding change) from context variables (pose, expression and quality change) using normal data only, then score the normalized residual. It shares the mechanism but no forensic signal. It provides a principled way to calibrate residuals by heteroscedastic variance, for example larger expected drift at extreme pose or low quality.

A.title: Flow-CAD: Flow Matching for Contextual Anomaly Detection and Explanation in Tabular Data
A.authors: (authors not shown in search snippet)
A.what_it_does: Learns a conditional generative model (flow matching) of behavioural features given context and scores anomalies by a normalized, truncated residual energy across behavioural dimensions.
A.overlap_explanation: A further adjacent-field instance of conditional residual scoring that could replace a plain regressor in Idea A (a conditional density of delta-identity given delta-nuisance). It is generic tabular work with no faces or video. It was seen only in a search snippet; the abstract was not read in full.

A.title: Protecting Celebrities from DeepFake with Identity Consistency Transformer (ICT)
A.authors: Xiaoyi Dong, Jianmin Bao, Dongdong Chen, Ting Zhang, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu, Dong Chen, Fang Wen, Baining Guo
A.what_it_does: Learns separate identity vectors for the inner and outer face regions with a transformer and flags a mismatch between them. ICT-Ref adds celebrity reference sets.
A.overlap_explanation: An identity-consistency forensic cue, but spatial (inner vs outer) and per-frame. It has no temporal or nuisance-conditioned modelling.

A.title: Micro-Expression-Aware Avatar Fingerprinting via Inter-Frame Feature Differencing
A.authors: Masoumeh Chapariniya, Jean-Marc Odobez, Volker Dellwo, Teodora Vuković
A.what_it_does: Avatar fingerprinting (who drives a talking head). It subtracts consecutive learned feature maps, so that static appearance cancels and only motion dynamics remain, then applies a SupCon temporal head. Feature-space differencing on a generic ResNet18 collapses, while a micro-motion backbone works.
A.overlap_explanation: Uses first-order differencing like TI2Net, but to remove identity and keep motion, the opposite of Idea A. It is useful evidence that differencing alone does not separate the factors.

A.title: Beyond Flicker: Detecting Kinematic Inconsistencies for Generalizable Deepfake Video Detection (KiMoI)
A.authors: Alejandro Cobo, Roberto Valle, José M. Buenaposada, Luis Baumela
A.what_it_does: Trains a landmark autoencoder with motion bases on real videos (CelebV-HQ). It perturbs those bases to create pseudo-fake videos whose cross-region facial motion correlations are broken, then trains a detector on them. It gains notably on DFD, DF40 reenactment and Wav2Lip.
