A.overlap_explanation: It learns a model of natural facial dynamics from real data and targets reenactment-style temporal artifacts. It does not use identity embeddings or a residual between an identity embedding and nuisance factors. It is a strong recent baseline for the reenactment weakness.

A.title: ID2image: Leakage of non-ID information into face descriptors and inversion from descriptors to images
A.authors: Mingrui Li, William A. P. Smith, Patrik Huber
A.what_it_does: Shows that pose, expression, landmarks, lighting and other non-ID attributes can be recovered from ArcFace and VGGFace2 embeddings almost as accurately as from the image.
A.overlap_explanation: Motivating evidence for Idea A: FR embeddings move with pose and expression, so raw temporal ArcFace differences (TI2Net) mix nuisance with forgery signal. It is not a detection method.

A.title: Unmasking Puppeteers: Leveraging Biometric Leakage to Expose Impersonation in AI-based Videoconferencing
A.authors: Samadi Vahdati, Nguyen, Nagano, Luebke, Gallo, Prashnani, Stamm
A.what_it_does: Detects puppeteering, where someone else drives a talking-head avatar. It re-encodes per-frame pose-and-expression latents into a low-dimensional 'biometric leakage' space. A pose-conditioned contrastive loss builds hard negatives of a different identity at the same pose, so the encoder keeps persistent identity cues and cancels transient pose and expression. Cosine scores against the reference are fused over time with an LSTM, and extreme-yaw frames are filtered out.
A.overlap_explanation: This is the closest work on the goal: identity evidence over time with the variation that pose and expression explain removed. The mechanism differs. It learns a pose-invariant embedding using pose-matched negatives, rather than predicting the expected change of an FR embedding from the change in nuisance factors and scoring the residual. The setting also differs: codec latents rather than ArcFace on RGB frames, a reference portrait is available, and the target is the driver's identity rather than real vs fake. It is the strongest baseline or alternative to discuss; its pose-matched negative trick could serve as an ablation against the residual-regression approach.

A.title: Detecting Deepfake Talking Heads from Facial Biometric Anomalies
A.authors: Norman, Farid
A.what_it_does: Reference-free detection. It computes ArcFace cosine similarities between all pairs of frames in a video and summarizes the distribution with 9 statistics (variance, skewness, kurtosis, quantiles, dispersion ratios), then classifies with XGBoost. Frames with pitch, yaw or roll above 25/20/20 degrees, or with an occluded face, are discarded. The authors attribute the low tail of the similarity distribution in fakes to large head motion.
A.overlap_explanation: It shares the signal: variation of FR identity embeddings within a video, with no reference. It handles pose only by hard-thresholding frames and does not model how much identity change pose or expression should cause. It still supports the motivation that identity variation in fakes depends on pose. Cross-dataset generalization is poor (FaceFusion to Celeb-DF v2 is near chance).

A.title: PIA: Deepfake Detection Using Phoneme-Temporal and Identity-Dynamic Analysis
A.authors: Datta, Ranga, Sun, Lyu
A.what_it_does: Audio-visual detector. One stream is ArcFace embeddings per frame. It argues that real videos show smooth consecutive ArcFace drift and that fakes show spikes in consecutive L2 distance. It adds an ArcFace temporal-consistency loss of the form 1 - cos(a_t, a_{t+1}), alongside phoneme/viseme and lip-geometry streams.
A.overlap_explanation: Like TI2Net, it uses raw consecutive differences of identity embeddings as the cue. It does not condition on pose, expression or quality, so this is the kind of unconditioned drift Idea A wants to correct. It is useful as recent evidence that the plain drift signal is still in use (2025).

A.title: Robust Deepfake Detection for Electronic Know Your Customer Systems Using Registered Images
A.authors: Amada, Kakizaki, Miyagawa, Ebihara, Shiohara, Yamasaki
A.what_it_does: Direct TI2Net extension: temporal differences of FR identity vectors (TDC) fed to a BiGRU with CE, triplet and anchor-positive loss. It adds an auxiliary difference against a registered genuine image (ADC). Swapping the frozen ArcFace extractor for AdaFace (quality-adaptive) trained on WebFace12M greatly improves cross-dataset AUC and robustness to degradation. Reports that TI2Net trained on KoDF is near chance cross-dataset.
A.overlap_explanation: It shares the TI2Net base and the quality-aware embedding component (AdaFace). It shows that a more quality-robust FR backbone suppresses false drift. It does not model identity change explained by nuisance factors. It is an essential baseline, and its AdaFace finding is a confound: part of Idea A's quality-nuisance benefit may come from simply using a better backbone, so ablations must control for it.

A.title: Exploring Static-Dynamic ID Matching and Temporal Static ID Inconsistency for Generalizable Deepfake Detection
A.authors: She, Hu, Liu, Li
A.what_it_does: Reference-free detection with two branches. One measures temporal anomalies of static ID: the per-frame face-recognition identity, in the TI2Net style. The other checks whether the clip-level static ID (appearance) matches the clip-level dynamic ID (facial behavior), trained with matching and constraint losses. The authors claim it detects both face swap and face reenactment and improves cross-dataset results.
A.overlap_explanation: It targets the same weakness as Idea A (TI2Net misses reenactment) and uses per-frame FR identity time series. It adds a behavior-vs-appearance consistency check rather than regressing identity drift on pose and expression change. A close competitor on the reenactment gap; compare with it directly. Judged from the abstract only.

A.title: It Wasn't Me: Irregular Identity in Deepfake Videos
A.authors: Liu, Bestagini, Huang, Zhou, Tubaro, Zhang, Yu
A.what_it_does: Trains a classifier on time series of facial identity features. The premise is that frame-by-frame generators make identity less stable over time in fakes. Targets interpretability and robustness on low-quality video.
A.overlap_explanation: Same family as TI2Net: an unconditioned identity time series with no nuisance modelling. A baseline that shares the signal but not the residual mechanism. Judged from the abstract.

A.title: Critical Contour Prior-Guided Graph Learning With Pose Calibration for Identity-Aware Deepfake Detection
A.authors: Ming, He, Li, Wang, Jiang
A.what_it_does: Reference-based identity-aware detection. It explicitly notes that head-pose variation degrades identity-consistency detectors. A graph attention network over contour-landmark features has a rotation-compensation block trained with pose-calibrated contrastive learning, which pulls features toward high-quality frontal faces. The similarity to reference samples gives the score.
A.overlap_explanation: It shares the explicit aim of removing pose-induced variation from identity evidence for deepfake detection. Its mechanism is a learned pose-compensated (frontalized) identity feature compared with references, not a temporal residual of FR-embedding change unexplained by pose, expression and quality. It needs reference samples. Judged from the abstract.

A.title: MOTIF: Person-of-Interest Deepfake Detection Beyond 3DMM Coefficients
A.authors: Affatato, Mandelli, Bestagini, Tubaro
A.what_it_does: Reference-based POI detector trained only on real VoxCeleb2. Per-frame 3DDFA-V3 coefficients (shape, expression, pose, translation) plus 3DMM lip vertices are fed to a temporal transformer with an identity-contrastive NT-Xent loss. Scoring uses whitened max-cosine against the reference set, with per-POI z-normalization. Ablations show that the shape block absorbs expression dynamics and that the coefficient groups are largely redundant.
A.overlap_explanation: It uses the same nuisance estimator family (3DMM pose and expression over time), trained on real videos only. Its whitening by reference variance is a form of normalizing for natural variability. It does not use FR embeddings or predict identity change from nuisance change, and it needs reference videos. Its finding that per-frame 3DMM fits entangle shape and expression is a practical warning for using 3DMM deltas as regressors.

A.title: ID-Reveal: Identity-aware DeepFake Video Detection
A.authors: Cozzolino, Rossler, Thies, Niessner, Verdoliva
A.what_it_does: Learns a temporal embedding of person-specific facial motion from 3DMM coefficient sequences using metric learning on real videos only, with an adversarial branch. It detects fakes by distance to reference videos of the claimed identity.
A.overlap_explanation: Seed paper. It shares the 3DMM temporal nuisance or behavior signal and real-only training, but it treats motion as the identity signal rather than as a nuisance to explain away FR-embedding drift. It needs references. Later work (eKYC, MOTIF) reports it is weak on reenactment and lip-sync.

A.title: Audio-Visual Person-of-Interest DeepFake Detection (POI-Forensics)
A.authors: Cozzolino, Pianese, Niessner, Verdoliva
A.what_it_does: Contrastively learns audio and visual identity embeddings on real talking-face videos and scores test videos against a POI reference set, with per-POI normalization.
A.overlap_explanation: Real-only, identity-based and reference-based. It does not model nuisance-explained identity drift. Related context only.

A.title: Detecting Deep-Fake Videos from Appearance and Behavior (A&B)
A.authors: Agarwal, El-Gaaly, Farid, Lim
A.what_it_does: Combines a static face-recognition biometric with a temporal behavioral embedding of expression and head movement, learned with metric learning. Detects face swaps when appearance identity and behavioral identity disagree.
A.overlap_explanation: Seed paper. It shares the idea of jointly using FR identity and pose/expression dynamics, but as two independent identity cues that are checked for agreement. It does not regress FR drift on nuisance change. Reference-based and focused on face swap.

A.title: ExposeAnyone: Personalized Audio-to-Expression Diffusion Models Are Robust Zero-Shot Face Forgery Detectors
A.authors: Shiohara, Yamasaki, Golyanik
A.what_it_does: Pre-trains an audio-to-FLAME-expression diffusion model on real video only, then personalizes it per POI with adapter tokens. The forgery score is the gap in diffusion reconstruction error with and without the identity adapter, i.e. how badly a conditional prediction explains the observed expression sequence. Clip-shared shape fitting disentangles shape from expression.
A.overlap_explanation: It shares the core statistical template: learn from real data a conditional model of what should be observed given a conditioning signal, then use the unexplained residual as the forgery score. Here the conditioning is audio and the target is expression; in Idea A the conditioning is the nuisance change and the target is FR-embedding change. Its clip-shared 3DMM shape trick is directly reusable. It needs references.

A.title: CUPID: Reconstructing UV Texture Maps for Interpretable Person-of-Interest Deepfake Detection
A.authors: Affatato, Mandelli, Cannas, Bestagini, Tubaro
A.what_it_does: Removes pose and expression by mapping faces into 3DMM UV texture space, then learns identity embeddings with an MAE plus contrastive loss on real videos only. For interpretability, it subtracts the reference-only displacement distribution from the test-vs-reference displacements, so it highlights only deviations not already explained by natural intra-reference variability.
A.overlap_explanation: It shares the goal of factoring out pose and expression before measuring identity, and of normalizing by natural (real) variability. It does this by geometric canonicalization rather than by predicting embedding change from nuisance change, and it is reference-based.

A.title: In Anticipation of Perfect Deepfake: Identity-anchored Artifact-agnostic Detection under Rebalanced Deepfake Detection Protocol (ID-Miner)
A.authors: Wang, Yeh, Chen, Yang, Chen
A.what_it_does: Encodes OpenFace action-unit sequences with an artifact-agnostic frame encoder and a GRU, trained with contrastive losses so that the embedding captures the identity of the person driving the motion, regardless of appearance or artifacts. Scores by cosine similarity to a reference.
A.overlap_explanation: Identity-from-behavior with a GRU, but no FR-embedding residual and no nuisance conditioning. Related context only.

A.title: Pose-Robust Face Recognition via Deep Residual Equivariant Mapping (DREAM)
A.authors: Cao, Rong, Li, Tang, Loy
A.code_available: yes (GitHub implementation listed on project page)
A.what_it_does: Adds a lightweight block that predicts a pose-dependent residual in deep FR feature space, gated by yaw. The residual maps profile-face embeddings to their frontal-equivalent location.
A.overlap_explanation: Adjacent field. It shows that the effect of pose on an FR embedding is a predictable, learnable residual: the 'expected embedding change given pose' half of Idea A. It can be transplanted directly as the nuisance-explanation module, or as a pre-normalization baseline before temporal differencing. It does no forensics or temporal modelling.

A.title: Attributes Shape the Embedding Space of Face Recognition Models
A.authors: Leroy, Mastropietro, Nurisso, Vaccarino
A.what_it_does: Analyzes FaceNet, ArcFace and AdaFace embeddings and shows that continuous attributes induce locally aligned vector fields inside each identity's point cloud. Pose and age are the least filtered out; illumination and contrast are the most. Proposes an invariance energy to measure this.
A.overlap_explanation: No detection. It provides empirical support that pose/expression-induced FR-embedding displacement is structured and locally predictable, which Idea A's regression assumes, and that ArcFace is least invariant to head angle.

A.title: ID2image: Leakage of Non-ID Information into Face Descriptors and Inversion from Descriptors to Images
A.authors: (Univ. of York; author metadata garbled in index)
A.what_it_does: Shows that pose, landmarks, lighting and other non-ID attributes can be predicted from ArcFace/VGGFace2 identity embeddings almost as accurately as from the image.
A.overlap_explanation: Motivation evidence: FR embeddings carry nuisance information, so raw consecutive differences, as in TI2Net, mix nuisance with identity change.

A.title: Micro-Expression-Aware Avatar Fingerprinting via Inter-Frame Feature Differencing
A.authors: Chapariniya, Odobez, Dellwo, Vukovic
A.what_it_does: Uses consecutive feature-map differencing (d_t = f_{t+1} - f_t) to cancel static appearance and keep the driver's motion dynamics, for avatar fingerprinting. Shows that differencing a generic ResNet18 feature collapses.
A.overlap_explanation: Uses the same first-order differencing as TI2Net, but to suppress appearance rather than to isolate identity, and without nuisance conditioning. Context for why plain differencing is insufficient.

A.title: Paired Geometric Supervision for Generalizable Deepfake Detection (OrthoPairGTL)
A.authors: Collins, Li, Nguyen, Sanchez
A.what_it_does: On a frozen DINOv3 backbone, models Real-to-Fake displacement in embedding space and trains a classifier to tell Real-to-Fake from Real-to-Real (benign) transformations. It penalizes large benign real-to-real variation and uses an ArcFace cross-check of the identity residual.
A.overlap_explanation: Conceptually related: it separates benign real-to-real embedding variation from manipulation displacement. However, it works frame-wise on generic features, is supervised with paired fakes, and has no pose, expression or quality conditioning.

B.title: Detecting Deepfake Talking Heads from Facial Biometric Anomalies
B.authors: Justin D. Norman, Hany Farid
B.what_it_does: Computes ArcFace (512-D) embeddings for every valid face frame in a video and takes the cosine similarity of all N(N-1)/2 frame pairs, which is the upper triangle of an identity TSM. It then reduces this to 9 distribution statistics (mean, variance, skew, kurtosis, quantiles, dispersion ratios) and classifies them with XGBoost. Tested on DeepSpeak face-swap and lip-sync, and on Celeb-DF-v2 (99.1% when trained in-domain, chance when trained cross-dataset).
B.overlap_explanation: Same signal (frozen ArcFace identity) and same core object (the full frame-by-frame pairwise identity similarity matrix) for deepfake detection. However, it throws away the 2D and temporal structure: it uses a histogram of all pairs with no time-gap encoding, no multi-lag strides, no geodesic velocity or acceleration, and no learned CNN or transformer over the matrix. It is still the closest prior art for the claim that all-pairs identity similarity beats consecutive differences. It needs long videos (about 2000 frames or more) and generalizes poorly across datasets.

B.title: ATSS: Detecting AI-Generated Videos via Anomalous Temporal Self-Similarity
B.authors: Hang Wang, Chao Shen, Lei Zhang, Zhi-Qi Cheng
B.what_it_does: Builds T x T temporal self-similarity matrices from cosine similarity of per-frame BLIP-2 visual embeddings, BLIP-2 caption-text embeddings, and a cross-modal visual-text matrix. Each matrix goes to its own Transformer encoder (each row is a frame token), the three are fused with bidirectional cross-attention, and an MLP classifies the result. Targets AI-generated video (GenVideo, EvalCrafter, VideoPhy, VidProM).
B.overlap_explanation: Same mechanism (full TSM of frozen per-frame embeddings, processed by a transformer, for forensic real/fake classification) with a different signal (generic BLIP-2 visual and text features, not face identity) and a different setting (whole-scene T2V/I2V generation, not face swap or reenactment). It uses plain cosine similarity, with no geodesic distance, multi-lag channels, time-gap encoding or velocity/acceleration. It will be the main reviewer comparison for the 'TSM + transformer' part of Idea B.

B.title: Compressed Deepfake Video Detection Based on 3D Spatiotemporal Trajectories
B.authors: Zongmei Chen, Xin Liao, Xiaoshuai Wu, Yanxiang Chen
B.what_it_does: Extracts 3D-landmark facial expression (AU-like distances and angles) and head-pose motion features per frame. It reconstructs phase-space trajectories with time-delay embedding, builds a recurrence plot (a thresholded L1-distance matrix between all time points), converts it to an adjacency matrix, and classifies it with a lightweight 2-layer Transformer, fused with Dempster-Shafer. It explicitly models first-frame-to-every-later-frame relations rather than only adjacent frames. Evaluated on FF++ HQ/LQ, Celeb-DF and DFDC.
B.overlap_explanation: Same mechanism family (a recurrence or self-similarity matrix over all frame pairs, learned by a transformer, for face deepfake detection) with a different signal (geometric facial motion and head pose, not identity embeddings). It uses binary thresholded recurrence rather than continuous geodesic similarity, and has no multi-lag or time-gap encoding and no hyperspherical velocity/acceleration.

B.title: Counting Out Time: Class Agnostic Video Repetition Counting in the Wild (RepNet)
B.authors: Debidatta Dwibedi, Yusuf Aytar, Jonathan Tompson, Pierre Sermanet, Andrew Zisserman
B.what_it_does: Computes a temporal self-similarity matrix (negative squared distances, softmax) from per-frame embeddings and forces the period predictor to read only the TSM, using a conv layer plus a transformer. This is the canonical TSM-to-CNN/transformer architecture.
B.overlap_explanation: Adjacent field (repetition counting) that uses exactly the proposed mechanism (TSM of per-frame embeddings processed by conv + transformer). Idea B is essentially 'RepNet-style TSM on ArcFace identity embeddings for forensics', so this must be cited as the architectural source. It is not forensic and has no identity, geodesic or multi-lag components.

B.title: TI2Net: Temporal Identity Inconsistency Network for Deepfake Detection
B.authors: Baoping Liu, Bo Liu, Ming Ding, Tianqing Zhu, Xin Yu
B.what_it_does: The baseline. Takes ArcFace identity vectors from 64 randomly sampled frames, computes first-order consecutive differences, encodes them with a GRU, and trains with CE + triplet loss + an anchor-positive distance term. Notably, its Fig. 1 motivates the method by showing a pairwise identity cosine-similarity matrix between frames (real vs fake), but the method then uses only consecutive differences.
B.overlap_explanation: The base paper already shows the pairwise identity similarity matrix as motivation, so reviewers may say the TSM is implicit in TI2Net. Idea B's novelty must lie in actually using the full matrix with geodesic distance, time-gap and multi-lag encoding, and a 2D learner. Its ablations are also relevant: random sampling beats sliding windows, which supports long-range lags.

B.title: Towards Robust DeepFake Detection under Unstable Face Sequences: Adaptive Sparse Graph Embedding with Order-Free Representation and Explicit Laplacian Spectral Prior (LR-GCN)
B.authors: Chih-Chung Hsu, Shao-Ning Chen, Mei-Hsuan Wu, Chia-Ming Lee, Yi-Fang Wang, Yi-Shiuan Chou
B.what_it_does: Builds an adaptive affinity matrix XX^T over spatial-temporal CNN feature nodes from all frames, thresholds it per node into a sparse graph, applies a graph-Laplacian high-pass prior followed by a GCN, and adds an L1 node-sparsity term. It is deliberately order-free for robustness to missing or shuffled faces (FF++, CDF2, DFDC).
B.overlap_explanation: Shares the 'all-pairs frame affinity matrix' component for face deepfake detection. However, it uses generic CNN patch features, inner-product affinity, and deliberately discards temporal order and time-gap information, which is the opposite of Idea B's explicit lag and time-gap encoding. Its stated limitation (it loses long-range temporal sequence anomalies) is a useful argument for Idea B.

B.title: AI-Generated Video Detection via Perceptual Straightening (ReStraV)
B.authors: Christian Internò, Robert Geirhos, Markus Olhofer, Sunny Liu, Barbara Hammer, David Klindt
B.what_it_does: Computes per-frame DINOv2 embeddings, then the stepwise distance (first-order 'velocity' magnitude) and curvature (the angle between successive displacement vectors, a second-order quantity) of the representation trajectory. Statistics of these feed a light classifier (MLP, RF and others) for AI-generated video detection.
B.overlap_explanation: Shares the 'velocity + curvature/acceleration of a per-frame embedding trajectory' component. It uses Euclidean geometry in DINOv2 space, not geodesic geometry on the ArcFace hypersphere, and has no TSM, no multi-lag and no face identity. It targets AIGV, not face swap or reenactment.

B.title: D3: Training-Free AI-Generated Video Detection Using Second-Order Features
B.authors: Zheng et al. (Xi'an Jiaotong Univ., OPPO, CityU HK)
B.what_it_does: Training-free AIGV detection using statistics of second-order central differences (acceleration) of per-frame features, derived from first-order inter-frame differences. The description comes from the listing and from MTOR's and ATSS's related-work summaries; the full text was not read.
B.overlap_explanation: Shares the second-order (acceleration) temporal-feature component. Different signal (generic visual features), no TSM, no identity, no hypersphere geometry, and a different setting (AIGV).

B.title: MTOR: Generalizable AI-Generated Video Detection with Multimodal Semantics and Temporal Over-Regularity
B.authors: Hang Wang, Chao Shen, Lei Zhang, Zhi-Qi Cheng
B.what_it_does: Its TOR branch computes six descriptors of temporal regularity from frozen visual tokens. These are the mean and std of adjacent frame-centroid cosine similarity, adjacent token correspondence, and frame-to-video stability (each frame vs all remaining frames: its std and mean absolute change). A linear head classifies them, fused with a caption-text branch.
B.overlap_explanation: Uses row-wise summaries of a frame-vs-all-frames similarity structure plus adjacent-similarity statistics, which overlaps with the TSM idea. It uses hand-crafted scalars, not a learned 2D model, generic visual tokens rather than identity, and has no multi-lag or geodesic geometry. Same group as ATSS, so they are actively working on self-similarity forensics.

B.title: PIA: Deepfake Detection Using Phoneme-Temporal and Identity-Dynamic Analysis
B.authors: Soumyya Kanti Datta, Tanvi Ranga, Chengzhe Sun, Siwei Lyu
B.what_it_does: Audio-visual detector fusing viseme crops, lip geometry and ArcFace embeddings with attention pooling. It adds an ArcFace temporal consistency loss (1 - cosine between consecutive frames) and motivates with consecutive-frame L2 identity drift plots (real smooth, face-swap spiky).
B.overlap_explanation: Shares the ArcFace consecutive-frame (lag-1) angular drift signal. It has no TSM, no multi-lag and no learned 2D processing, and identity is only one stream in a multimodal model.

B.title: Exploiting Style Latent Flows for Generalizing Deepfake Video Detection (StyleFlow / StyleGRU)
B.authors: Jongwook Choi, Taehoon Kim, Yonghyun Jeong, Seungryul Baek, Jongwon Choi
B.what_it_does: Extracts pSp StyleGAN W+ latents per frame and computes first-order 'style flow' differences, encoded by a bidirectional GRU trained with triplet + BCE (structurally close to TI2Net). A style attention module fuses this with 3D-ResNet (FTCN) content features. Supplementary Table 6 compares no differencing, first-order and second-order differencing (89.0 vs 88.8 vs 88.4 on CDF).
B.overlap_explanation: Same paradigm as TI2Net (consecutive differences of a frozen face latent, GRU, triplet loss) and already tests second-order differencing, finding little gain. That weakens a novelty claim for acceleration alone. It has no TSM, no multi-lag and no geodesic geometry.

B.title: It Wasn't Me: Irregular Identity in Deepfake Videos
B.authors: Honggu Liu, Paolo Bestagini, Lin Huang, Wenbo Zhou, Stefano Tubaro, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu
B.what_it_does: Interpretable detector trained on time series of facial identity features, motivated by identity features being less stable over time in deepfakes. It targets low-quality deepfakes and unseen datasets. Only the abstract was seen.
B.overlap_explanation: Same signal (temporal identity-feature instability). From the abstract there is no evidence of a TSM, multi-lag or geodesic modeling. The full method was not verified.

B.title: Exploring Static-Dynamic ID Matching and Temporal Static ID Inconsistency for Generalizable Deepfake Detection
B.authors: Huimin She, Yongjian Hu, Beibei Liu, Chang-Tsun Li
B.what_it_does: Two-branch, reference-free detector. One branch checks static-ID (appearance) vs dynamic-ID (behavior) mismatch; the other detects temporal anomaly of image-level static IDs. It claims to detect both face replacement and face reenactment. Only the abstract was seen.
B.overlap_explanation: Shares the temporal static-identity inconsistency component and explicitly targets reenactment, TI2Net's weak spot. The TSM, multi-lag and geodesic components were not seen in the abstract. It is a direct competitor on the 'identity cues for reenactment' claim.

B.title: Exploring High-Order Self-Similarity for Video Understanding
B.authors: POSTECH / RLWRLD / INRIA authors (listing only)
B.what_it_does: Extends space-time self-similarity (STSS: visual correspondences across frames as a motion representation) to higher-order self-similarity for video understanding. Only the listing and abstract snippet were seen.
B.overlap_explanation: Adjacent-field reference for learned (higher-order) self-similarity representations of video. Could support the 'multi-order TSM' design, but it is not forensic and not identity-based.

B.title: TRACE: Trajectory Representation and Consistency Estimation for AI-Generated Video Detection
B.authors: Huangsen Cao, Hongkang Chu, Siyao Yu, Xin Ding, Jianfeng Dong, Yongwei Wang
B.what_it_does: Probes a frozen Wan2.2 video DiT at several flow times to get per-frame velocity responses, computes adjacent-frame velocity differences, and trains with BCE plus a real-centered pull/push objective (EMA real center).
B.overlap_explanation: Only shares adjacent-frame differences and a real-centered compactness loss, which resembles TI2Net's anchor-positive regularizer. Different signal and setting, and no TSM.

B.title: Deepfake detection in videos with multiple faces using geometric-fakeness features
B.authors: Kirill Vyshegorodtsev, Dmitry Kudiyarov, Alexander Balashov, Alexander Kuzmin
B.what_it_does: Uses FaceNet embedding distances between adjacent frames only to track and group faces. It then builds per-face matrices of per-frame fakeness scores and face-area features, processed by a multi-kernel CNN.
B.overlap_explanation: Identity embeddings are used only for tracking, not as the forensic signal, and there is no self-similarity matrix.

B.title: VoD: Learning Volume of Differences for Video-Based Deepfake Detection
B.authors: Ying Xu, Marius Pedersen, Kiran Raja
B.what_it_does: Feeds pixel-level consecutive frame differences into X3D-S. Ablations show that larger sampling intervals (strides 2-6) and first-frame-referenced differences (SSFF) both hurt compared with stride-1 consecutive differences. It compares against TI2Net (CDF2 72.4 vs 68.2).
B.overlap_explanation: Pixel domain, not identity. Its negative result on larger strides and first-frame references is a counterpoint the multi-lag design should address in ablations.

B.title: ID-Reveal: Identity-aware DeepFake Video Detection
B.authors: Davide Cozzolino, Andreas Rössler, Justus Thies, Matthias Nießner, Luisa Verdoliva
B.what_it_does: Learns person-specific temporal facial-motion embeddings from 3DMM sequences with metric learning and adversarial training, using only real videos. It compares test snippets against a pristine reference set via minimum pairwise distances. Notably strong on reenactment.
B.overlap_explanation: Identity-dynamics context and a reenactment benchmark competitor. It is reference-based and has no TSM of identity embeddings.

B.title: Detecting Deepfake Talking Heads from Facial Biometric Anomalies
B.authors: Justin D. Norman, Hany Farid
B.what_it_does: Extracts ArcFace 512-D embeddings for every valid face frame, computes cosine similarity for ALL N(N-1)/2 frame pairs (i.e., the full identity self-similarity matrix), summarizes the distribution of pairwise similarities with 9 statistics (mean, variance, skew, kurtosis, quantiles, dispersion ratios) and classifies with XGBoost. Reports face-swap fakes show bimodal/broader pairwise identity similarity than real videos. Evaluated on DeepSpeak (FaceFusion variants, lip-sync) and Celeb-DF-v2; poor cross-dataset transfer (FaceFusion->CDF ~48% acc) without retraining.
B.overlap_explanation: Same core signal as Idea B: the frame-by-frame pairwise identity (ArcFace) similarity matrix used for reference-free deepfake detection. Differences: it treats the matrix as an unordered bag of similarities (histogram moments), discarding temporal structure, time-gap/lag information, multi-stride analysis, velocity/acceleration, geodesic distance, and any learned 2D CNN/transformer over the matrix. This is the single most important prior to cite and differentiate against.

B.title: ATSS: Detecting AI-Generated Videos via Anomalous Temporal Self-Similarity
B.authors: Hang Wang, Chao Shen, Lei Zhang, Zhi-Qi Cheng
B.what_it_does: Builds T x T temporal self-similarity matrices (cosine) from BLIP-2 visual embeddings, caption text embeddings, and a cross-modal visual-text matrix; each matrix is tokenized row-wise (each row = a frame token) and encoded by a dedicated Transformer, then fused with bidirectional cross-attention and an MLP. Targets text/image-to-video AIGV detection (GenVideo, EvalCrafter, VideoPhy, VidProM).
B.overlap_explanation: Same mechanism (explicit full TSM of per-frame embeddings processed by a learned Transformer for forgery detection) but a different signal (generic visual/semantic features, not identity) and setting (fully generated scenes, not face swap/reenactment). No multi-lag strides, time-gap encoding, geodesic distance or sphere velocity/acceleration. Directly undermines any claim that 'TSM for video forensics' is new; novelty must rest on identity-specific TSM, multi-scale lags, hyperspherical geometry and face-reenactment generalization.

B.title: TI2Net: Temporal Identity Inconsistency Network for Deepfake Detection
B.authors: Baoping Liu, Bo Liu, Ming Ding, Tianqing Zhu, Xin Yu
B.what_it_does: Base paper: frozen face-recognition identity vectors per frame, first-order temporal differences, GRU, triplet + CE loss. Its figure visualizes pair-wise identity similarities between frames for real (lower triangle) vs fake (upper triangle) videos.
B.overlap_explanation: The baseline being upgraded. Notably it already visualizes the pairwise identity similarity matrix as motivation, but only uses lag-1 differences as model input. Reviewers will expect the new paper to show that learning on the full matrix and multi-lag structure beats what TI2Net already plotted.

B.title: Robust Deepfake Detection for Electronic Know Your Customer Systems Using Registered Images
B.authors: Takuma Amada, Kazuya Kakizaki, Taiki Miyagawa, Akinori F. Ebihara, Kaede Shiohara, Toshihiko Yamasaki
B.what_it_does: Direct TI2Net extension: Temporal Difference Comparison (consecutive identity-vector differences, as TI2Net) plus Auxiliary Difference Comparison (each frame's identity vector minus a registered reference image's vector), concatenated into an RNN with CE + triplet + anchor-positive losses; shows a stronger face recognizer (AdaFace on WebFace12M) greatly improves robustness and that the reference branch helps face reenactment (FOMM, audio-driven).
B.overlap_explanation: Shares the identity-embedding temporal-inconsistency pipeline and explicitly targets TI2Net's reenactment weakness, but via a reference image rather than a self-similarity matrix; still only lag-1 differences, no TSM, no multi-scale lags or sphere geometry. Important competing 'TI2Net upgrade' and a source for the backbone-swap ablation (ArcFace vs AdaFace).

B.title: PIA: Deepfake Detection Using Phoneme-Temporal and Identity-Dynamic Analysis
B.authors: Soumyya Kanti Datta, Tanvi Ranga, Chengzhe Sun, Siwei Lyu
B.what_it_does: Audio-visual detector combining phoneme-aligned viseme crops, lip geometry and ArcFace identity embeddings; motivates with consecutive-frame ArcFace L2 drift being spikier for face swaps, and adds an ArcFace temporal consistency loss (1 - cosine between consecutive frames).
B.overlap_explanation: Uses consecutive-frame ArcFace identity drift (lag-1 angular/cosine distance) as a cue and loss; no pairwise TSM, no multi-lag, multimodal (audio) setting.

B.title: Towards Robust DeepFake Detection under Unstable Face Sequences: Adaptive Sparse Graph Embedding with Order-Free Representation and Explicit Laplacian Spectral Prior (LR-GCN)
B.authors: Chih-Chung Hsu, Shao-Ning Chen, Mei-Hsuan Wu, Chia-Ming Lee, Yi-Fang Wang, Yi-Shiuan Chou
B.what_it_does: Builds an adaptive affinity matrix XX^T over all spatio-temporal CNN feature nodes across frames (order-free), sparsifies it by adaptive thresholding, applies a Laplacian high-pass prior and GCN for face deepfake detection (FF++, CDF-v2, DFDC), robust to missing/shuffled frames.
B.overlap_explanation: Uses a cross-frame feature affinity (similarity) matrix as the core structure for face-forgery video detection, but on appearance CNN features (not identity), deliberately order-free (opposite of explicit time-gap encoding), and processed by GCN rather than a 2D CNN over a TSM.

B.title: MTOR: Generalizable AI-Generated Video Detection with Multimodal Semantics and Temporal Over-Regularity
B.authors: Hang Wang, Chao Shen, Lei Zhang, Zhi-Qi Cheng
B.what_it_does: Same group as ATSS. Six temporal descriptors from frozen visual tokens: mean/std of adjacent-frame centroid cosine similarity, mean/std of adjacent token correspondence, and std / mean-absolute-change of frame-to-rest-of-video similarity; linear head fused with a caption-based multimodal branch.
B.overlap_explanation: Hand-crafted statistics of adjacent and frame-to-video similarity (row summaries of a TSM) for AIGV detection; no identity features, no learned TSM encoder, no multi-lag. Shows the 'similarity-structure' line is active in 2026.

B.title: Compressed Deepfake Video Detection Based on 3D Spatiotemporal Trajectories
B.authors: Zongmei Chen, Xin Liao, Xiaoshuai Wu, Yanxiang Chen
B.what_it_does: Extracts 3D-model-based facial action/landmark and head-pose features, reconstructs phase-space trajectories via time-delay embedding, builds recurrence plots (binary all-pairs state-similarity matrices) and feeds them to a lightweight Transformer; targets compressed FF++/CDF/DFDC.
B.overlap_explanation: A recurrence plot is a thresholded temporal self-similarity matrix used for face deepfake detection; signal is geometric/expression motion features, not identity embeddings, and lacks multi-scale lags, geodesic distances, or identity velocity/acceleration. Must be cited as prior use of RP/TSM in face forensics.

B.title: AI-Generated Video Detection via Perceptual Straightening (ReStraV)
B.authors: Interno et al. (Bielefeld University, Google DeepMind, Honda Research Institute EU, CSHL)
B.what_it_does: Treats per-frame DINOv2 embeddings as a trajectory and classifies statistics of temporal curvature (angle between successive displacement vectors) and stepwise distance; based on the perceptual straightening hypothesis.
B.overlap_explanation: Shares the 'velocity (step distance) + curvature/acceleration of an embedding trajectory' component of Idea B, but for generic AIGV with DINOv2 features, not identity on the ArcFace hypersphere, and without a TSM.

B.title: D3: Training-Free AI-Generated Video Detection Using Second-Order Features
B.authors: Zheng et al. (Xi'an Jiaotong University, OPPO, CityU HK)
B.what_it_does: Training-free AIGV detector derived from Newtonian-mechanics intuition: computes second-order central differences of per-frame features (acceleration of the feature trajectory) and uses their statistics to separate real from generated videos.
B.overlap_explanation: Shares the 2nd-order (acceleration) dynamics component; different signal (generic visual features), different setting (AIGV), no TSM or identity.

B.title: Exploiting Style Latent Flows for Generalizing Deepfake Video Detection (StyleGRU / StyleFlow)
B.authors: Jongwook Choi, Taehoon Kim, Yonghyun Jeong, Seungryul Baek, Jongwon Choi
B.what_it_does: Extracts pSp StyleGAN style latents per frame, computes first-order 'style flow' differences, encodes with a bidirectional GRU trained with supervised contrastive (triplet) + BCE, fuses with 3D-ResNet content features via style attention and a temporal transformer. Supplementary ablation compares no differencing vs 1st- vs 2nd-order differencing (1st best, small gaps).
B.overlap_explanation: Architecturally the closest sibling of TI2Net (differences of a frozen face latent + GRU + triplet) on a different latent; it already tested 2nd-order differences, which weakens a novelty claim on 'velocity/acceleration' alone. No pairwise TSM or multi-lag.

B.title: MARS: Multiscale Appearance-Residual Streams for Video Forgery Detection
B.authors: Ahmed Y. Radwan, Shaina Raza
B.code_available: Yes (models and code released per paper)
B.what_it_does: Applies fixed spatial and temporal difference-of-Gaussians at multiple scales (tau in {0.5,1,2,4}) plus first differences to frozen PE-Core features, models them with a temporal transformer, and gates with a LayerNorm-tuned semantic path; covers both face manipulations and generated video. Cites TI2Net and StyleFlow as related.
B.overlap_explanation: Shares the multi-scale temporal differencing idea (multiple temporal bands beyond lag-1) on frozen features; not identity, not a pairwise TSM, Euclidean rather than geodesic.

B.title: It Wasn't Me: Irregular Identity in Deepfake Videos
B.authors: Honggu Liu, Paolo Bestagini, Lin Huang, Wenbo Zhou, Stefano Tubaro, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu
B.what_it_does: Observes facial identity features are less temporally stable in deepfakes because generators work frame-by-frame; trains a detector on time series of facial identity features, reporting robustness on low-quality videos and promising cross-dataset results.
B.overlap_explanation: Concurrent identity-time-series detector (same family as TI2Net); per abstract it models identity sequences rather than a self-similarity matrix or multi-lag geometry (full text not read).

B.title: Exploring Static-Dynamic ID Matching and Temporal Static ID Inconsistency for Generalizable Deepfake Detection
B.authors: Huimin She, Yongjian Hu, Beibei Liu, Chang-Tsun Li
B.what_it_does: Two-branch reference-free detector: (1) discrepancy between clip-level static ID (appearance) and dynamic ID (facial behavior), (2) temporal anomaly of image-level static IDs; claims detection of both face replacement and face reenactment and better unseen-dataset generalization.
B.overlap_explanation: Shares temporal static-identity inconsistency and explicitly addresses the reenactment gap that TI2Net (and Idea B's motivation) targets; abstract-level only, no evidence of TSM/multi-lag/hypersphere geometry.

B.title: DCNN-Based Deepfake Detection Using a Fused Model
B.authors: S. Naga Raju, Darbhasayanam Shreeya, Lade Prashanth, Samudrala Prashanthi, Aleti Kiran
B.what_it_does: Extracts InceptionResnetV1 face embeddings per frame, temporally pools them for statistical features, and adds an interpretable logistic regression on internal identity similarity between frames; fused with a meta-classifier on Celeb-DF.
B.overlap_explanation: Uses inter-frame identity similarity statistics for video-level detection (a summary of the identity TSM); low-impact venue, no structured TSM learning, multi-lag or geodesic dynamics.

B.title: Detecting AI-Generated Video via Frame Consistency (DeCoF)
B.authors: Ma et al. (USTC)
B.what_it_does: Uses frozen CLIP frame embeddings and learns inter-frame consistency (decoupling spatial artifacts) to detect generated videos across generators.
B.overlap_explanation: Frozen-encoder inter-frame consistency as the forensic cue, but not identity, no explicit TSM, multi-lag or sphere geometry.

B.title: Exploring Temporal Coherence for More General Video Face Forgery Detection (FTCN)
B.authors: Yinglin Zheng, Jianmin Bao, Dong Chen, Ming Zeng, Fang Wen
B.code_available: Yes (official FTCN repo is widely used; weights reused by StyleFlow)
B.what_it_does: Fully temporal convolution network with spatial kernel size 1 plus a temporal transformer to learn temporal coherence from raw face crops.
B.overlap_explanation: Seed 'temporal coherence' detector; pixel-level temporal modeling, no identity embeddings or self-similarity matrices. Standard baseline.

B.title: AltFreezing for More General Video Face Forgery Detection
B.authors: Wang et al. (USTC)
B.code_available: Yes (released checkpoints referenced by later works)
B.what_it_does: 3D-ConvNet detector that alternately freezes spatial and temporal weights so the model learns both spatial and temporal artifacts; strong cross-manipulation baseline.
B.overlap_explanation: Seed temporal detector and baseline; no identity, TSM, or trajectory geometry.

B.title: Exploring High-Order Self-Similarity for Video Understanding
B.authors: POSTECH / RLWRLD / INRIA Grenoble authors
B.what_it_does: Extends space-time self-similarity (STSS) representations to higher-order self-similarity for video recognition, learning from correspondence/similarity volumes across frames.
B.overlap_explanation: Adjacent field (action recognition) technique for learning on self-similarity tensors that could be transplanted as the TSM encoder; no forensics.

B.title: SphereVAD: Training-Free Video Anomaly Detection via Geodesic Inference on the Unit Hypersphere
B.authors: Sun Yat-sen University / HIT authors
B.what_it_does: Training-free video anomaly detection that performs geodesic inference on L2-normalized (unit hypersphere) features.
B.overlap_explanation: Adjacent-field precedent for using hyperspherical geodesic distances on normalized embeddings over video; transplantable for the 'angular/geodesic identity distance' component; not deepfake or identity.

F.title: UniForensics: Face Forgery Detection via General Facial Representation (Dynamic Video Self-Blending, DVSB)
F.authors: Ziyuan Fang, Hanqing Zhao, Tianyi Wei, Wenbo Zhou, Ming Wan, Zhanyi Wang, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu
F.what_it_does: Builds video pseudo-fakes from real face videos only, using Dynamic Video Self-Blending (DVSB). Every SBI-style parameter group K(t) (colour, quality, blending dislocation, mask, mask deformation, blending blur) gets a random per-frame sequence, which is then Gaussian-filtered in the DCT domain. The forgery trace therefore drifts smoothly over time instead of being fixed or white-noise jitter. The backbone is a UniFormerV2 initialised from the FaRL face encoder, so the features are rich in identity and semantics. Training is a two-stage contrastive pretraining plus fine-tuning. The ablation shows low-frequency time-varying blending beats both the static and the independent-per-frame versions.
F.overlap_explanation: This is the closest prior work to Idea F part (2). It already publishes 'self-blending with temporally varying parameters to create temporal jitter, using only real videos', and it ablates the frequency of the variation. Differences: it self-blends rather than blending in a different identity, and its detector is a pixel-level spatio-temporal transformer, not a GRU or forecaster on ArcFace embedding trajectories. Reviewers will treat DVSB as the direct baseline for any 'temporal SBI' claim.
F.code_available: Not stated in the pages read

F.title: Vulnerability-Aware Spatio-Temporal Learning for Generalizable Deepfake Video Detection (FakeSTormer, Self-Blended Video SBV)
F.authors: Dat Nguyen, Marcella Astrid, Anis Kacem, Enjie Ghorbel, Djamila Aouada
F.what_it_does: Extends SBI to video as Self-Blended Video. SBI parameters stay constant across frames, and landmark interpolation keeps the blend temporally coherent with deliberately small residual errors. Trains a multi-task TimeSformer on FF++ real videos plus SBV only, with temporal and spatial 'vulnerability' heads. Reports CDF 92.8, DFD 98.6 and DFDCP 90.2 AUC without any fake data.
F.overlap_explanation: Same core idea as part (2): video-level self-blended pseudo-fakes and fake-free training of a temporal detector. The blend strength is kept constant rather than varied, there is no identity swap, and the detector is pixel-based. It sets the fake-free video SOTA that Idea F's numbers (TI2Net: CDF2 68.2) would be compared against.
F.code_available: Yes, https://github.com/10Ring/FakeSTormer

F.title: Beyond Flicker: Detecting Kinematic Inconsistencies for Generalizable Deepfake Video Detection (KiMoI)
F.authors: Alejandro Cobo, Roberto Valle, Jose M. Buenaposada, Luis Baumela
F.what_it_does: Trains an autoencoder (Landmark Perturbation Network) on real landmark-motion sequences (consecutive differences). It perturbs the learned motion bases to break natural correlations between facial regions, then morphs real frames to match, producing temporal pseudo-fakes. These are combined with SBI spatial pseudo-fakes to train a MARLIN ViT on real data only. Reports SOTA among pristine-only methods and strong DF40 Wav2Lip (reenactment) results. Directly compares against CBI (AltFreezing) and VB.
F.overlap_explanation: Same mechanism as part (2): synthesise temporal pseudo-fakes from real videos only, using a model of natural facial dynamics learned from real data, which also touches part (1). It explicitly targets reenactment, TI2Net's stated weakness. The signal differs: landmark kinematics rather than identity embeddings, and pixel morphing rather than identity blending.
F.code_available: Paper says code will be released upon publication

F.title: Generalizing Deepfake Video Detection with Plug-and-Play: Video-Level Blending and Spatiotemporal Adapter Tuning (VB + StA)
F.authors: Zhiyuan Yan, Yandan Zhao, Shen Chen, Mingyi Guo, Xinghe Fu, Taiping Yao, Shouhong Ding, Li Yuan
F.what_it_does: Identifies 'Facial Feature Drift' (frame-to-frame jitter of facial organs in deepfakes). Video-level Blending (VB) simulates it: affine perturbations to each frame's organ landmarks, sampled independently per frame, followed by self-blending. A CLIP model with spatiotemporal adapters is trained on this data. Compares against CBI and PFIG alternatives.
F.overlap_explanation: Synthesises temporal jitter pseudo-fakes from real frames by per-frame self-blending with randomly varying parameters, which is the same mechanism as part (2). The jitter is geometric (organ drift) rather than identity, and the signal is pixel-level rather than ArcFace embeddings.
F.code_available: Not stated in the pages read

F.title: Detecting Deepfake by Creating Spatio-Temporal Regularity Disruption (P-fake Generator + STE)
F.authors: Jiazhi Guan, Hang Zhou, Mingming Gong, Errui Ding, Jingdong Wang, Youjian Zhao
F.what_it_does: Generates pseudo-fake videos from real videos only. A Random Parameter Generator samples a new set of edit, mask and blend parameters for each frame (held fixed over randomly chosen consecutive runs), producing temporal regularity disruption through blend-after-edit. A ResNet with spatio-temporal enhancement blocks is trained on real data plus p-fakes and beats SBI on Deepwild and DFDCP.
F.overlap_explanation: An early instance of 'self-blending with temporally varying parameters gives temporal pseudo-fakes without deepfake data', which is the core of part (2). No identity source and no identity-embedding detector.
F.code_available: Not stated in the pages read

F.title: Unsupervised Multimodal Deepfake Detection Using Intra- and Cross-Modal Inconsistencies
F.authors: Mulin Tian, Mahyar Khayatkhoei, Joe Mathai, Wael AbdAlmageed
F.what_it_does: Trained only on real VoxCeleb2 videos. Per-frame AdaFace identity features pass through a temporal transformer per window. An intra-modal contrastive loss makes identity windows from the same video similar and windows from different people dissimilar. At test time the T x T identity-similarity matrix within a video gives the fake score, with no reference needed. It also adds an audio-visual cross-modal score and gives an information-theoretic argument that identity or motion inconsistency is unavoidable.
F.overlap_explanation: Same signal and setting as part (1): face-recognition identity embeddings over time, trained on real data only, scored as an anomaly by temporal identity inconsistency. The mechanism differs: contrastive self-similarity instead of masked or next-step forecasting with prediction error. Strong prior art for 'real-only identity-trajectory anomaly detection'.
F.code_available: Not stated in the pages read

F.title: Self-Supervised Video Forensics by Audio-Visual Anomaly Detection (AVAD)
F.authors: Chao Feng, Ziyang Chen, Andrew Owens
F.what_it_does: Trains an autoregressive model on time-delay audio-visual synchronisation features from real, unlabeled videos only. At test time, videos the model assigns low probability (anomalies) are flagged as manipulated.
F.overlap_explanation: Same mechanism as part (1): sequence modelling of a feature trajectory on real-only data, with prediction likelihood or error as the anomaly score. The signal differs (audio-visual sync rather than identity embeddings). Idea F(1) would read as 'AVAD transplanted to ArcFace trajectories' unless the difference is clearly argued.
F.code_available: Yes, https://github.com/cfeng16/audio-visual-forensics

F.title: Spotting Deepfakes by Learning Real Human Motion: A Self-Supervised Temporal Consistency Framework for Robust Deepfake Detection
F.authors: Anchal Kanojiya
F.what_it_does: A CNN extracts per-frame facial features and an LSTM or Transformer predicts future frame representations from past ones, learning authentic motion. Detection uses prediction inconsistency as the anomaly indicator, aiming to reduce dependence on fake datasets.
F.overlap_explanation: Same mechanism as part (1): forecast the next representation on real video and use prediction error as the anomaly score. Its features are generic CNN features rather than frozen identity embeddings. It is a low-visibility venue and the abstract gives no benchmarks, but it is prior art on the mechanism.
F.code_available: Not stated

F.title: Learning Natural Consistency Representation for Face Forgery Video Detection (NACO)
F.authors: Daichi Zhang, Zihao Xiao, Shikun Li, Fanzhao Lin, Jianmin Li, Shiming Ge
F.what_it_does: Self-supervised pretraining on real VoxCeleb2 videos only. Per-frame CNN features go into a Transformer, with a Spatial Predictive Module (masked frame-feature prediction, MSE) and a Temporal Contrastive Module (frame-shuffled clips as negatives). The backbone is then frozen and an MLP head is fine-tuned on FF++ real and fake data.
F.overlap_explanation: Shares the masked-trajectory-modelling component of part (1): masked per-frame feature prediction learned from real videos. But it uses generic CNN features rather than identity embeddings, and detection is a supervised head, not prediction error. The frame-shuffle negatives are a crude temporal pseudo-fake.
F.code_available: Not stated in the pages read

F.title: Next-Frame Feature Prediction for Multimodal Deepfake Detection and Temporal Localization
F.authors: Ashutosh Anshul, Shreyas Gopal, Deepu Rajan, Eng Siong Chng
F.what_it_does: Causal transformer encoder and decoder modules predict the next frame's visual, audio and cross-modal features. Local convolutional attention compares predicted and actual features, and the discrepancy feeds classification and temporal localisation. Training is single-stage on real plus fake data with a contrastive loss that pulls predicted and actual features together for real frames and apart for fakes.
F.overlap_explanation: Shares the next-step feature-forecasting and prediction-discrepancy component of part (1), but it is supervised with fakes and uses generic AV-HuBERT-style features, not identity embeddings.
F.code_available: Not stated in the pages read

F.title: Generalizing Video DeepFake Detection by Self-generated Audio-Visual Pseudo-Fakes (AVPF)
F.authors: Zihe Wei, Yuezun Li
F.what_it_does: Creates pseudo-fakes from authentic videos only. Audio-Visual Self-Blending blends a temporally shifted copy of one modality into the original with a time-varying blending factor alpha_t (windowed and triangular-smoothed) inside a facial mask. Audio-Visual Self-Splicing splices similar snippets from the same video. Trains on real data plus AVPF, beating real-only AVH-Align.
F.overlap_explanation: Shares the 'time-varying blend strength alpha_t from real data only' component of part (2), but in the audio-visual lip domain with self-sourced content rather than a different identity.
F.code_available: Yes, https://github.com/OUC-VAS/AVPF

F.title: AltFreezing for More General Video Face Forgery Detection
F.authors: Zhendong Wang, Jianmin Bao, Wengang Zhou, Weilun Wang, Houqiang Li
F.what_it_does: Alternately freezes the spatial and temporal weights of a 3D CNN. Adds video-level augmentation: temporal dropout and repeat, plus clip-level blending (CBI), which blends faces from two clips frame by frame to create temporal artifacts. Trained with FF++ fakes plus the augmentations.
F.overlap_explanation: Its video-level data augmentation (CBI) is a pseudo-fake video synthesis that injects temporal inconsistency, one ingredient of part (2). It is not fake-free, does not vary blend strength, and has no identity-embedding detector.
F.code_available: Not stated in the pages read

F.title: Does an Illumination Prior Help Face-Swap Detection? A Controlled Study of Temporal Self-Blended Images (T-SBI)
F.authors: Danil Davydov, Bader Rasheed, Dmitriy Vatolin
F.what_it_does: Defines 'Temporal Self-Blended Images': it transfers the illumination statistics of one frame onto a self-blended copy of another frame from the same video. Trains a frame-level EfficientNet-B4 and reports a mostly null effect, apart from a threshold shift and better robustness to heavy compression.
F.overlap_explanation: Uses the name 'temporal SBI' and builds pseudo-fakes across two frames of one video, but the detector is frame-level and the artifact is photometric, not identity jitter. Relevant mainly because it already claims the 'Temporal SBI' name and reports negative results for a naive temporal extension.
F.code_available: Not stated

F.title: ID-Reveal: Identity-aware DeepFake Video Detection
F.authors: Davide Cozzolino, Andreas Rossler, Justus Thies, Matthias Niessner, Luisa Verdoliva
F.what_it_does: Learns temporal facial features from 3DMM expression and pose sequences that capture how a person moves when talking. Uses metric learning plus adversarial training on real videos only. At test time it compares the embedding against a reference video of the claimed identity.
F.overlap_explanation: Real-only training on temporal identity-behaviour trajectories, with anomaly-style distance scoring, which is one component of part (1). The signal is 3DMM motion rather than ArcFace appearance identity, it needs a reference, and it does no forecasting.
F.code_available: Not stated in the pages read

F.title: In Anticipation of Perfect Deepfake: Identity-anchored Artifact-agnostic Detection under Rebalanced Deepfake Detection Protocol (ID-Miner)
F.authors: Wei-Han Wang, Chin-Yuan Yeh, Hsi-Wen Chen, De-Nian Yang, Ming-Syan Chen
F.what_it_does: Generates 'self-deepfakes' from genuine videos with a white-hat reenactment model (FOMM). Trains a FAU-feature encoder plus GRU with an artifact-agnostic frame-level contrastive loss and an identity-anchored video-level contrastive loss. Detection uses reference-based cosine similarity, and TI2Net is among the baselines.
F.overlap_explanation: Uses a GRU over per-frame identity-related trajectories and synthesises training negatives from real data with a generator, loosely related to both parts. But it needs a reference, uses action units rather than identity embeddings, and does not use time-varying blending or forecasting.
F.code_available: Anonymous repo cited in paper (anonymous.4open.science/r/idminer-7F15)

F.title: Robust Deepfake Detection for Electronic Know Your Customer Systems Using Registered Images
F.authors: Takuma Amada, Kazuya Kakizaki, Taiki Miyagawa, Akinori F. Ebihara, Kaede Shiohara, Toshihiko Yamasaki
F.what_it_does: Directly extends TI2Net. It keeps TI2Net's temporal difference vectors (Temporal Difference Comparison), adds differences against a registered genuine image (Auxiliary Difference Comparison), feeds both to an RNN with CE + triplet + anchor-positive loss, and swaps ArcFace for WebFace12M AdaFace. Trained supervised on KoDF. Shows that random frame sampling generalises better than a sliding window.
F.overlap_explanation: A published TI2Net upgrade by the SBI authors, so it competes directly on the 'upgrade TI2Net' framing. It does not use self-supervised forecasting or pseudo-fakes, which is the space Idea F occupies. Useful as a baseline and for its finding that a stronger face-recognition backbone helps.
F.code_available: Yes, https://github.com/TaikiMiyagawa/DeepfakeDetection4eKYC

F.title: Protecting Celebrities from DeepFake with Identity Consistency Transformer (ICT)
F.authors: Xiaoyi Dong, Jianmin Bao, Dongdong Chen, Ting Zhang, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu, Dong Chen, Fang Wen, Baining Guo
F.what_it_does: Trains on real face-recognition data only (MS1MV2). Synthesises fake-like samples by swapping faces between different real identities, so inner and outer face identities differ, and learns to detect inner/outer identity inconsistency. An optional reference identity set is supported.
F.overlap_explanation: Shares the 'blend in a different identity from real data to make identity-inconsistent pseudo-fakes, no deepfake generator needed' component of part (2). It is image-level (spatial inner/outer inconsistency) with no temporal variation of blend strength.
F.code_available: Not stated in the pages read

F.title: Exploring Static-Dynamic ID Matching and Temporal Static ID Inconsistency for Generalizable Deepfake Detection
F.authors: Huimin She, Yongjian Hu, Beibei Liu, Chang-Tsun Li
F.what_it_does: A reference-free detector with two branches. One checks consistency between clip-level static identity (appearance) and dynamic identity (behaviour). The other detects temporal anomalies in image-level static identity embeddings. Claims it handles both face swapping and reenactment.
F.overlap_explanation: Same signal as TI2Net and Idea F (temporal anomaly of static identity embeddings), with an added behavioural-identity branch aimed at reenactment. Supervised, with no forecasting or pseudo-fake synthesis.
F.code_available: Not stated

F.title: Leveraging Real Talking Faces via Self-Supervision for Robust Forgery Detection (RealForensics)
F.authors: Alexandros Haliassos, Rodrigo Mira, Stavros Petridis, Maja Pantic
F.what_it_does: Self-supervised cross-modal (audio-visual) pretraining on real talking-face videos learns temporally dense visual representations. These then guide a visual forgery detector trained with FF++ fakes.
F.overlap_explanation: Learns natural face dynamics from real videos only as a prior, as Idea F intends. But detection is supervised with real fakes, the signal is audio-visual and lip-centric rather than identity trajectories, and it uses no forecasting error or pseudo-fakes.
F.code_available: Not stated in the pages read

F.title: Learning Regularity in Skeleton Trajectories for Anomaly Detection in Videos (MPED-RNN)
F.authors: Romero Morais, Vuong Le, Truyen Tran, et al.
F.what_it_does: Learns normal human motion from skeleton trajectories, decomposed into global and local components, with a message-passing encoder-decoder RNN. It reconstructs and predicts trajectories, and the error gives the anomaly score. Trained on normal data only.
F.overlap_explanation: An adjacent field (video anomaly detection) whose technique transplants directly to part (1): one-class forecasting or reconstruction of a low-dimensional per-frame trajectory, scored by prediction error. Not deepfake-specific.
F.code_available: Not stated

F.title: Holistic Representation Learning for Multitask Trajectory Anomaly Detection
F.authors: Alexandros Stergiou, Brent De Weerdt, Nikos Deligiannis
F.what_it_does: An attention-based encoder-decoder learns expected skeleton-trajectory motion by reconstructing any masked continuous temporal segment (past extrapolation, future extrapolation, in-between interpolation). Trained on normal data, with reconstruction error used for anomaly detection.
F.overlap_explanation: An adjacent-field version of 'masked trajectory modelling, anomaly = prediction error' on low-dimensional per-frame trajectories, almost exactly the recipe of part (1) applied to skeletons rather than identity embeddings.
F.code_available: Not stated

F.title: UniForensics: Face Forgery Detection via General Facial Representation (Dynamic Video Self-Blending, DVSB)
F.authors: Ziyuan Fang, Hanqing Zhao, Tianyi Wei, Wenbo Zhou, Ming Wan, Zhanyi Wang, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu
F.what_it_does: Extends SBI to video by sampling SBI parameters per frame (color, quality, blending offset, mask, mask deformation, and blur/blend strategy), then low-pass filtering that parameter sequence in time with a DCT-domain Gaussian filter. The result is a pseudo-fake video whose forgery strength varies smoothly over time. A FaRL face encoder with a UniFormerV2 temporal transformer is trained first with contrastive 'forgery process identification' on DVSB samples, then fine-tuned. Ablation: static < independent per-frame < low-frequency dynamic.
F.overlap_explanation: This is close to component (2): a video SBI in which blend parameters vary over time, with an explicit study of the jitter spectrum (static vs. white noise vs. smoothed). Differences: it self-blends the same identity (no injected foreign identity), it works in pixel space on a spatio-temporal backbone rather than on identity-embedding trajectories, and it has no real-only predictive objective. A new paper must cite it, and must frame its own blending as cross-identity, identity-level jitter measured in ArcFace space.

F.title: Generalizing Video DeepFake Detection by Self-generated Audio-Visual Pseudo-Fakes (AVPF)
F.authors: Zihe Wei, Yuezun Li
F.what_it_does: Trains on real VoxCeleb2 videos plus pseudo-fakes only. Visual self-blending blends the face (convex-hull mask with elastic deformation) with a time-shifted copy of the same video. A per-frame blend factor alpha_t in [0,1] comes from temporal window masks smoothed by a triangular kernel. It also does audio self-blending and audio-visual self-splicing of similar snippets. AV-HuBERT backbone, binary classifier.
F.overlap_explanation: Uses the same mechanism as component (2): a temporally varying blend strength alpha_t applied to real videos, which creates localized temporal inconsistency without generator data. The signal differs (a time-shifted self rather than a different identity; lip ROI and audio-visual), and there is no identity-embedding modelling. It shows that 'temporal blend-strength jitter on real-only data' was already in the literature in 2026.

F.title: Unsupervised Multimodal Deepfake Detection Using Intra- and Cross-Modal Inconsistencies
F.authors: Mulin Tian, Mahyar Khayatkhoei, Joe Mathai, Wael AbdAlmageed
F.what_it_does: Trained only on real VoxCeleb2. Per-frame AdaFace identity features are aggregated by a transformer per time window. An intra-modal contrastive loss pulls together the identity features of the same video across windows. At test time the T x T identity-similarity matrix within a video gives a fakeness score (n-th percentile). An audio-visual cross-modal branch is added. It also gives an information-theoretic argument that deepfakes must trade identity consistency against motion transfer.
F.overlap_explanation: This is the closest prior work for component (1): real-only, anomaly scoring of a face-recognition identity trajectory within a single video, with no reference video. It uses contrastive self-similarity instead of next/masked-embedding prediction, and it has no pseudo-fakes. The intra-modal (visual identity) score alone is weak on FakeAVCeleb (about 78 AUC), which is consistent with TI2Net's weakness on reenactment.

F.title: Self-Supervised Video Forensics by Audio-Visual Anomaly Detection (AVAD)
F.authors: Chao Feng, Ziyang Chen, Andrew Owens
F.what_it_does: Trains an autoregressive transformer on real videos only (LRS2/LRS3) to predict the next frame's audio-visual synchronization features (time-delay distributions or activations). Videos with high prediction loss (low likelihood) are flagged as fake.
F.overlap_explanation: Same mechanism as component (1): real-only autoregressive forecasting of a per-frame feature trajectory, with prediction error as the anomaly score. The signal differs (audio-visual sync features rather than identity embeddings), and it needs audio. A direct seed paper; part (1) transplants this to ArcFace trajectories.

F.title: Spotting Deepfakes by Learning Real Human Motion: A Self-Supervised Temporal Consistency Framework for Robust Deepfake Detection
F.authors: Anchal Kanojiya
F.what_it_does: Proposes self-supervised detection that learns authentic motion by predicting future frame representations (CNN features, LSTM or Transformer) from past ones, and uses prediction inconsistency as the anomaly score.
F.overlap_explanation: Same predict-the-next-representation anomaly idea, visual-only and trained on real data, but with generic CNN appearance features rather than identity embeddings, and no pseudo-fakes. Low-visibility venue, and I only saw the abstract, but it still prevents a claim of 'first visual real-only forecasting detector'.

F.title: Learning Natural Consistency Representation for Face Forgery Video Detection (NACO)
F.authors: Daichi Zhang, Zihao Xiao, Shikun Li, Fanzhao Lin, Jianmin Li, Shiming Ge
F.what_it_does: Self-supervised pretraining on real VoxCeleb2 face videos. Per-frame CNN features go into a Transformer, with a Spatial Predictive Module that reconstructs randomly masked frame features (MSE) and a Temporal Contrastive Module that uses frame-shuffled clips as negatives. An MLP head is then fine-tuned on FF++ real/fake.
F.overlap_explanation: Shares masked-feature-trajectory modelling on real videos only (component 1), but the features are learned appearance features rather than frozen identity embeddings. It is used as pretraining plus a supervised head, not as an anomaly score.

F.title: Vulnerability-Aware Spatio-Temporal Learning for Generalizable Deepfake Video Detection (FakeSTormer, Self-Blended Video SBV)
F.authors: Dat Nguyen, Marcella Astrid, Anis Kacem, Enjie Ghorbel, Djamila Aouada
F.what_it_does: Real-only training with Self-Blended Videos: SBI parameters (including blending ratio) are fixed from the first frame and reused for all frames, landmark interpolation keeps the result coherent, and vulnerability-driven cutout is added. A TimeSformer has auxiliary spatial and temporal vulnerability heads. Code: github.com/10Ring/FakeSTormer.
F.overlap_explanation: A video analogue of SBI, which is the framing of component (2). It deliberately keeps blend parameters constant over time (the opposite of jitter) and uses no identity features. A key baseline for 'temporal SBI'.

F.title: Generalizing Deepfake Video Detection with Plug-and-Play: Video-Level Blending and Spatiotemporal Adapter Tuning (VB / StA)
F.authors: Zhiyuan Yan, Yandan Zhao, Shen Chen, Mingyi Guo, Xinghe Fu, Taiping Yao, Shouhong Ding, Li Yuan
F.what_it_does: Identifies Facial Feature Drift (FFD) and simulates it with Video-level Blending: random affine warps of facial organs, self-blended independently in each frame. These are used as pseudo-fake videos for a CLIP model with spatio-temporal adapters. Also compares clip blending (CBI) and PFIG variants.
F.overlap_explanation: Real-only video pseudo-fakes with frame-to-frame jitter (component 2), but the jitter is geometric warping of the same identity, not identity mixing, and no identity embeddings or prediction objective are used.

F.title: Beyond Flicker: Detecting Kinematic Inconsistencies for Generalizable Deepfake Video Detection (KiMoI)
F.authors: Alejandro Cobo, Roberto Valle, Jose M. Buenaposada, Luis Baumela
F.what_it_does: Trains a landmark-sequence autoencoder on CelebV-HQ to learn motion bases, perturbs basis weights with per-timestep noise to break inter-region motion correlations, and morphs pristine videos to follow the perturbed landmarks. These temporal pseudo-fakes plus SBI train a MARLIN ViT on pristine data only. Strong on DFD, DFo and Wav2Lip reenactment.
F.overlap_explanation: Learns natural facial dynamics from real video and synthesizes temporal pseudo-fakes without generator data, which matches the philosophy of both components. The signal is landmark kinematics rather than identity, with no identity mixing and no anomaly scoring. Relevant because it targets reenactment, TI2Net's weak point.

F.title: Does an Illumination Prior Help Face-Swap Detection? A Controlled Study of Temporal Self-Blended Images (T-SBI)
F.authors: Danil Davydov, Bader Rasheed, Dmitriy Vatolin
F.what_it_does: Builds self-blended pairs from two frames of the same video, transferring one frame's illumination onto the self-blended copy of another (gated by the LAB luminance difference). It finds a null effect on the targeted illumination mechanism, but a threshold shift and better compression robustness. EfficientNet-B4, frame-level.
F.overlap_explanation: The name 'Temporal SBI' is already taken in the literature. Its mechanism (cross-frame photometric self-blending) differs from identity jitter, but it should be cited, and its negative result is a cautionary data point.

F.title: AltFreezing for More General Video Face Forgery Detection (clip-level blending, CBI)
F.authors: Zhendong Wang, Jianmin Bao, Wengang Zhou, Weilun Wang, Houqiang Li
F.what_it_does: Alternately freezes the spatial and temporal kernels of a 3D CNN. Adds video-level augmentations: temporal dropout, temporal repeat, and clip-level blending, where a foreground clip (possibly from another video/identity) is blended into a background clip with the same mask over the whole clip.
F.overlap_explanation: A seed paper for the idea. CBI blends a potentially different identity at video level, which is part of component (2), but the blend is constant over time (no strength jitter), and the training still uses real FF++ fakes.

F.title: Detecting Deepfake by Creating Spatio-Temporal Regularity Disruption (STC / Pseudo-fake Generator)
F.authors: Jiazhi Guan, Hang Zhou, Mingming Gong, Youjian Zhao, Errui Ding, Jingdong Wang
F.what_it_does: A Pseudo-fake Generator disrupts the spatial and temporal regularity of real videos (including frame shuffling) to train detectors without fake videos, plus a Spatio-Temporal Enhancement block.
F.overlap_explanation: Real-only video pseudo-fakes for temporal detectors (component 2's setting), but the disruptions are not identity blending with time-varying strength.

F.title: ID-Reveal: Identity-aware DeepFake Video Detection
F.authors: Davide Cozzolino, Andreas Rossler, Justus Thies, Matthias Niessner, Luisa Verdoliva
F.what_it_does: Learns temporal facial-motion embeddings from 3DMM expression/pose sequences on real videos only (metric learning plus an adversarial 3DMM generator). At test time it compares against reference videos of the claimed person.
F.overlap_explanation: Real-only temporal identity/behaviour modelling (component 1's spirit), strong on reenactment. It needs reference videos, uses 3DMM motion rather than ArcFace identity embeddings, and uses a distance to references rather than prediction error.

F.title: Next-Frame Feature Prediction for Multimodal Deepfake Detection and Temporal Localization
F.authors: Ashutosh Anshul, Shreyas Gopal, Deepu Rajan, Eng Siong Chng
F.what_it_does: Causal transformer encoder/decoder modules predict next-frame unimodal (visual, audio) and cross-modal features. Local convolutional cross-attention compares predicted and actual features. A contrastive loss pulls predicted and actual features together for real samples and pushes them apart for fakes. Trained end-to-end with fakes.
F.overlap_explanation: Shares next-frame feature forecasting with the prediction discrepancy as the cue. It is supervised (needs fakes), uses AV-HuBERT-style features rather than identity, and has no pseudo-fakes.

F.title: Detecting Deepfake Talking Heads from Facial Biometric Anomalies
F.authors: Justin D. Norman, Hany Farid
F.what_it_does: Computes pairwise ArcFace cosine similarities across all frames of a video, summarizes their distribution with 9 statistics (skew, kurtosis, quantiles, dispersion ratios), and classifies with XGBoost. Finds that face-swaps have both anomalously large and anomalously small identity variation.
F.overlap_explanation: Same signal (the distribution of ArcFace identities within a video, reference-free), but supervised on fakes with hand-crafted statistics. It offers no forecasting or pseudo-fakes. Its finding that some fakes are 'too stable' matters for jitter design.

F.title: PIA: Deepfake Detection Using Phoneme-Temporal and Identity-Dynamic Analysis
F.authors: Soumyya Kanti Datta, Tanvi Ranga, Chengzhe Sun, Siwei Lyu
F.what_it_does: A multimodal supervised detector fusing viseme crops, lip geometry, and ArcFace embeddings. Adds an ArcFace temporal-consistency auxiliary loss on consecutive-frame cosine drift. Code: github.com/skrantidatta/PIA.
F.overlap_explanation: Uses ArcFace temporal drift (as TI2Net does), but supervised, multimodal, with no real-only modelling or pseudo-fakes.

F.title: It Wasn't Me: Irregular Identity in Deepfake Videos
F.authors: Honggu Liu, Paolo Bestagini, Lin Huang, Wenbo Zhou, Stefano Tubaro, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu
F.code_available: https://github.com/HongguLiu/Identity-Inconsistency-DeepFake-Detection
F.what_it_does: Trains a detector on time series of facial identity features, based on the observation that identity features are less temporally stable in deepfakes. Targets low-quality videos.
F.overlap_explanation: A concurrent TI2Net-like identity time-series classifier (supervised, judging from the abstract). Relevant context only; no forecasting or pseudo-fakes.

F.title: Exploring Static-Dynamic ID Matching and Temporal Static ID Inconsistency for Generalizable Deepfake Detection
F.authors: Huimin She, Yongjian Hu, Beibei Liu, Chang-Tsun Li
F.what_it_does: Reference-free identity-anomaly detector with two branches: static (appearance) vs. dynamic (behaviour) ID mismatch, and temporal inconsistency of per-frame static IDs. Claims to detect reenactment as well as swaps.
F.overlap_explanation: Upgrades TI2Net-style temporal static-ID inconsistency and addresses reenactment, but (from the abstract) it is supervised, with no real-only forecasting or synthetic identity jitter. Should be cited as an identity-based competitor.

F.title: Leveraging Real Talking Faces via Self-Supervision for Robust Forgery Detection (RealForensics)
F.authors: Alexandros Haliassos, Rodrigo Mira, Stavros Petridis, Maja Pantic
F.what_it_does: Audio-visual self-supervised pretraining on real talking faces (LRW), then supervised forgery detection on FF++ with a visual-only network.
F.overlap_explanation: A seed paper: it learns natural facial dynamics from real video, but through AV correspondence pretraining plus supervised fine-tuning. No identity embeddings, forecasting anomaly score, or pseudo-fakes.

F.title: Detecting Deepfakes with Self-Blended Images (SBI)
F.authors: Kaede Shiohara, Toshihiko Yamasaki
F.what_it_does: Creates pseudo-fakes by blending a pristine image with a transformed copy of itself, and trains a detector on real images plus SBIs only.
F.overlap_explanation: The image-level source of component (2). It has no temporal dimension and no cross-identity blending.

F.title: Leveraging Trajectory Prediction for Pedestrian Video Anomaly Detection
F.authors: (University of Michigan authors; see arXiv page)
F.what_it_does: Video anomaly detection that forecasts pedestrian trajectories from normal data and uses the trajectory prediction error as the anomaly score.
F.overlap_explanation: An adjacent-field template for component (1): forecasting a per-entity trajectory trained on normal data, with prediction error as the anomaly score. It could be transplanted directly to ArcFace embedding trajectories. (Skeleton-VAD diffusion/flow methods such as MoCoDAD, arXiv 2307.07205, belong to the same family.)

D.title: MOTIF: Person-of-Interest Deepfake Detection Beyond 3DMM Coefficients
D.authors: Giovanni Affatato, Sara Mandelli, Paolo Bestagini, Stefano Tubaro
D.code_available: Announced at polimi-ispl/MOTIF (paper says it will be released)
D.what_it_does: Fits a 3DMM (3DDFA-V3) to each frame and gets 80 shape, 64 expression and 6 pose/translation coefficients.
