A temporal transformer trained with identity-contrastive NT-Xent on real VoxCeleb2 videos encodes 75-frame windows of these. A second part-level branch encodes the reconstructed lip vertices (968 vertices, temporal mean removed) with its own temporal transformer. The global and mouth scores are fused after per-POI calibration against reference videos. The ablation shows the shape block read over time recovers almost all of the accuracy, and reading it dynamically helps most on reenactment. The mouth branch adds +9.1 AUC on FakeAVCeleb lip-sync and +3.6 on KoDF reenactment. Evaluated on face swap, reenactment (LivePortrait, FOMM, etc.) and lip-sync.
D.overlap_explanation: Closest prior work. It already models per-frame 3DMM shape-coefficient trajectories plus a separate part-level (mouth) 3D trajectory, fuses them, and explicitly targets reenactment and lip-sync, which keep global identity. Differences from Idea D: (1) it is reference-based (POI enrollment), not a reference-free binary detector trained on FF++; (2) the only region is the mouth, and its conclusion says other facial regions 'remain to be explored'; (3) it has no per-region ArcFace-style identity embeddings and no temporal differencing, GRU or triplet setup. It also warns that per-frame shape coefficients absorb expression dynamics, which directly affects the 3DMM half of Idea D.

D.title: Mining Temporal Inconsistency with 3D Face Model for Deepfake Video Detection
D.authors: Ziyi Cheng, Chen Chen, Yichao Zhou, Xiyuan Hu
D.what_it_does: Fits a 3D face model to each frame. Per frame it uses the 2D-landmark vs 3D-reprojection Euclidean distances plus the 3D shape and texture features, and an RNN models the sequence. It reports strong cross-manipulation results.
D.overlap_explanation: Same core mechanism as the 3DMM half of Idea D: per-frame 3DMM shape features, reference-free, temporal RNN for deepfake detection. It has no per-region identity embeddings, and it is framed around face swapping rather than reenactment or lip-sync.

D.title: Exploring Static-Dynamic ID Matching and Temporal Static ID Inconsistency for Generalizable Deepfake Detection
D.authors: Huimin She, Yongjian Hu, Beibei Liu, Chang-Tsun Li
D.what_it_does: A reference-free identity-based video detector with two branches. One checks the mismatch between a clip-level static ID (appearance) and a dynamic ID (facial behaviour). The other checks the temporal inconsistency of image-level static IDs. It adds a static-dynamic ID matching loss and a dynamic ID constraint loss, and explicitly claims to detect both face replacement and face reenactment.
D.overlap_explanation: Shares the motivation (fixing TI2Net-style global identity's weakness on reenactment, reference-free) and the temporal static-ID branch. It uses global face identity plus a behaviour ID, not part- or region-level identity or 3DMM shape trajectories.

D.title: ID-Reveal: Identity-aware DeepFake Video Detection
D.authors: Davide Cozzolino, Andreas Rossler, Justus Thies, Matthias Niessner, Luisa Verdoliva
D.what_it_does: Extracts 3DMM parameters per frame. A Temporal ID Network, trained adversarially with a 3DMM generative network and only on real videos, embeds facial motion. A test video is compared against reference videos of the same person. Reports more than 15% accuracy gains on facial reenactment under high compression.
D.overlap_explanation: Temporal 3DMM trajectories used to catch reenactment, but reference-based (POI) and based on global coefficients. No part-level identity and no supervised real-vs-fake training.

D.title: Video deepfake detection using a hybrid CNN-LSTM-Transformer model for identity verification
D.authors: G. Petmezas, V. Vanian, K. Konstantoudakis, E. E. I. Almaloglou, D. Zarpalas
D.what_it_does: Feeds per-frame 3DMM features into a CNN-LSTM-Transformer to model short- and long-term temporal dynamics. Uses identity verification against reference videos, trained on pristine VoxCeleb2 only.
D.overlap_explanation: Temporal modelling of 3DMM coefficients for identity-based detection. It is reference-based, uses global coefficients and has no regional identity.

D.title: Within 3DMM Space: Exploring Inherent 3D Artifact for Video Forgery Detection (3DAD)
D.authors: Chunlei Peng, Tianmin Xu, Decheng Liu, Nannan Wang, Xinbo Gao
D.what_it_does: A 3D Analysis Unit is pre-trained on 3DMM face reconstruction to give high-level 3D representations. A Texture Perception Unit extracts low-level texture. Both are fused in a spatio-temporal model to find spatio-temporal inconsistency in 3DMM semantic space.
D.overlap_explanation: Reference-free temporal inconsistency in 3DMM space, matching the 3DMM-trajectory component of Idea D. It treats the face globally, with no part-level identity embeddings or triplet identity setup.

D.title: Face Forgery Detection Based on Facial Region Displacement Trajectory Series (FTDN)
D.authors: YuYang Sun, ZhiYong Zhang, Isao Echizen, Huy H. Nguyen, ChangZhen Qiu, Lu Sun
D.what_it_does: Defines 7 facial ROIs from landmarks and tracks virtual-anchor displacements per ROI with forward-backward optical flow, giving 28 features x 64 frames. A dual-stream spatial-temporal graph attention network plus a GRU encoder classifies, with a reconstruction auxiliary loss. Graph attention helps most on Face2Face and NeuralTextures.
D.overlap_explanation: Region-level temporal trajectories (multiple facial parts modelled jointly with GRU and graph attention), including gains on reenactment. The per-region signal is geometric displacement, not identity embeddings or 3DMM shape.

D.title: Improving the Efficiency and Robustness of Deepfakes Detection through Precise Geometric Features (LRNet)
D.authors: Zekun Sun, Yujie Han, Zeyu Hua, Na Ruan, Weijia Jia
D.what_it_does: Calibrated facial-landmark sequences feed a two-stream GRU: one stream on landmark positions/shape, the other on frame-to-frame landmark differences. Robust to compression.
D.overlap_explanation: Same temporal design as TI2Net plus first-order differences, but over facial geometry (landmarks of eyes, nose, mouth and contour) instead of identity. It is an obvious baseline for the geometric or part branch of Idea D. There are no identity or 3DMM shape embeddings.

D.title: Protecting Celebrities from DeepFake with Identity Consistency Transformer (ICT)
D.authors: Xiaoyi Dong, Jianmin Bao, Dongdong Chen, et al.
D.what_it_does: Learns separate identity vectors for the inner face and outer face with a transformer and a consistency loss, and flags identity inconsistency between them. An optional reference set enhances it.
D.overlap_explanation: Region-level identity (inner vs outer) consistency, the spatial half of Idea D. It is frame-level with no temporal trajectories, and it targets face swaps; reenactment and lip-sync keep both regions' identity.

D.title: RAIRNet: Region-Aware Identity Rectification for Face Forgery Detection
D.authors: Mingqi Fang, Lingyun Yu, Hongtao Xie, Junqiang Wu, Zezheng Wang, Jiahong Li, Yongdong Zhang
D.what_it_does: Argues that forged identity is hybrid and regionally distributed, so a single global ID vector misses local identity inconsistency. A generic identity extractor branch plus a bias-diminishing branch rectify the identity bias. A meta-learned identity filter generator produces region-aware filters to find locally inconsistent identity regions, and adaptive weighting balances local and global.
D.overlap_explanation: Explicitly motivates local/regional identity inconsistency over global identity, which is a core premise of Idea D. It is image-level (no temporal trajectories) and uses learned region filters rather than per-part embeddings over time. Follow-up IEIRNet (IEEE TMM 2024) is similar.

D.title: Robust Deepfake Detection for Electronic Know Your Customer Systems Using Registered Images
D.authors: Takuma Amada, Kazuya Kakizaki, Taiki Miyagawa, Akinori F. Ebihara, Kaede Shiohara, Toshihiko Yamasaki
D.what_it_does: A direct TI2Net extension. It keeps temporal differences of face-recognition embeddings (TDC) and adds differences to a registered reference image (ADC), with an RNN, CE, triplet and anchor-positive losses, and a stronger AdaFace/WebFace12M extractor. Ablations show TDC alone is weaker on reenactment, while the reference branch fixes FOMM and audio-driven reenactment.
D.overlap_explanation: Shares the full TI2Net pipeline and the goal of fixing reenactment. It solves it with a reference image rather than part-level identity, and confirms that global temporal identity struggles on reenactment. This is a competing TI2Net upgrade that must be compared against.

D.title: PIA: Deepfake Detection Using Phoneme-Temporal and Identity-Dynamic Analysis
D.authors: Soumyya Kanti Datta, Tanvi Ranga, Chengzhe Sun, Siwei Lyu
D.what_it_does: An audio-visual detector. It fuses per-frame global ArcFace embeddings (with an ArcFace temporal-consistency loss on consecutive cosine drift), MediaPipe lip-geometry (mouth aspect ratio) and mouth-crop 3D-CNN features, selected by phoneme. Evaluated on lip-sync, face-swap and avatar subsets of FakeAVCeleb and DeepSpeak v2.0.
D.overlap_explanation: Combines global identity drift over time with a mouth-region geometric stream to cover lip-sync. Identity is global and needs audio; there are no per-region identity embeddings or 3DMM shape.

D.title: Detecting Deepfake Talking Heads from Facial Biometric Anomalies
D.authors: Justin D. Norman, Hany Farid
D.what_it_does: Computes the distribution of pairwise ArcFace cosine similarities across all frames of a video. Nine moment features go into XGBoost, which is reference-free. It works on face swaps and, when trained on them, on lip-sync (97.1%), but generalises poorly to Celeb-DF.
D.overlap_explanation: Temporal identity-embedding (in)consistency applied to lip-sync. It uses only the global face embedding and no part-level identity.

D.title: Landmark-Guided Local Temporal Modeling for Deepfake Video Detection
D.authors: Yu-Cheng Gu
D.what_it_does: Extends facial-component-guided CLIP adaptation with a landmark-guided local temporal branch. Component-specific patch masks for eyes, nose and lips let component queries attend to CLIP features inside each region over time.
D.overlap_explanation: Per-facial-component temporal modelling (eyes, nose, lips), which matches the regional-temporal structure of Idea D. The features are CLIP appearance features rather than identity embeddings or 3DMM shape. Only the abstract was seen.

D.title: Towards More General Video-based Deepfake Detection through Facial Component Guided Adaptation for Foundation Model (DFD-FCG)
D.authors: Yue-Hua Han, Tai-Ming Huang, Kai-Lung Hua, Jun-Cheng Chen
D.what_it_does: A side-network decoder with spatial and temporal modules on a frozen CLIP ViT. A facial-component guidance loss steers learnable queries to major facial parts. Strong cross-dataset video AUC.
D.overlap_explanation: Facial-part-guided spatio-temporal video detector; a strong modern baseline. It is appearance-based, with no identity or 3DMM trajectories.

D.title: Mover: Mask and Recovery based Facial Part Consistency Aware Method for Deepfake Video Detection
D.authors: Juan Hu, Xin Liao, Difei Gao, et al.
D.venue_year: arXiv 2023 (related DeepfakeMAE by the same authors)
D.what_it_does: Randomly masks facial-part ROIs and reconstructs them, using recoverability to learn facial-part consistency, for example smiling eyes versus an upset mouth in reenactment.
D.overlap_explanation: Shares the premise that manipulations break consistency between facial parts, especially expression or reenactment. It uses masked reconstruction, not part-level identity trajectories.

D.title: Region-Aware Temporal Inconsistency Learning for DeepFake Video Detection (RATF)
D.authors: Zhihao Gu, Taiping Yao, Yang Chen, et al.
D.what_it_does: A Region-Aware Temporal Filter module generates separate temporal filters for different spatial regions, so each region learns its own temporal inconsistency.
D.overlap_explanation: Region-specific temporal inconsistency, but on learned CNN feature maps rather than semantic facial-part identity or shape.

D.title: Exposing Lip-syncing Deepfakes from Mouth Inconsistencies (LIPINC)
D.authors: Soumyya Kanti Datta, Shan Jia, Siwei Lyu
D.what_it_does: Detects lip-sync deepfakes from local and global spatial-temporal inconsistencies of the mouth region across frames.
D.overlap_explanation: Mouth-region temporal inconsistency for lip-sync, one region of Idea D. It is appearance-based, with no identity embedding or multi-region joint modelling.

D.title: Lips Don't Lie: A Generalisable and Robust Approach to Face Forgery Detection (LipForensics)
D.authors: Alexandros Haliassos, Konstantinos Vougioukas, Stavros Petridis, Maja Pantic
D.what_it_does: A lip-reading-pretrained spatio-temporal network on mouth crops detects mouth-movement anomalies and generalises well, including to reenactment.
D.overlap_explanation: A strong part-specific (mouth) temporal baseline that Idea D must beat on reenactment and lip-sync. It does not use identity embeddings.

D.title: Interpretable Deepfake Detection in Videos via Explicit Forensic Features and Temporal Modeling
D.authors: Chahira Benhama, Mohand Said Allili, Assia Hamadene
D.what_it_does: Builds identity-consistent face tracks, computes 68 hand-crafted per-frame features (photometric, texture, geometric and compression, some regional: mouth, jaw, hair contour, left/right halves) and feeds them to an LSTM.
D.overlap_explanation: Region-aware per-frame descriptors modelled over time with an RNN. These are hand-crafted forensic statistics, not identity or 3DMM shape.

I.title: Unsupervised Multimodal Deepfake Detection Using Intra- and Cross-Modal Inconsistencies
I.authors: Mulin Tian, Mahyar Khayatkhoei, Joe Mathai, Wael AbdAlmageed
I.code_available: not stated in the parts read
I.what_it_does: Splits a video into T fixed-length time windows. An AdaFace-based identity network gives one identity vector per window, and the T x T similarity matrix of those vectors is the intra-modal identity-consistency score. A visual network and a Whisper audio network give per-window features, trained contrastively so that audio and video from the same window match; the diagonal of that audio-visual similarity matrix is the cross-modal score. The two scores are added. Trained only on real VoxCeleb2 videos, it reports 96.8 average AUC on FakeAVCeleb and also tests on KoDF.
I.overlap_explanation: Closest in structure. It builds a per-window face-identity trajectory, checks how consistent it stays over time, and adds a per-window audio-visual comparison. The difference: its audio-visual branch compares audio with facial motion (synchrony), not speaker-identity embeddings with face-identity embeddings. It never compares a voice-identity trajectory with a face-identity trajectory and does not model drift (first-order differences).

I.title: Audio-Visual Person-of-Interest DeepFake Detection (POI-Forensics)
I.authors: Davide Cozzolino, Alessandro Pianese, Matthias Niessner, Luisa Verdoliva
I.what_it_does: Trains a ResNet-50 audio identity encoder and a ResNet-50 video identity encoder on real VoxCeleb2 3-second segments, with single-modality and joint audio-video contrastive losses. At test time, each 3 s segment's audio, video and joint embeddings are compared with a reference set of real videos of the same person. The normalized similarities are averaged over segments to decide real or fake.
I.overlap_explanation: Same core signal: per-window voice-identity and face-identity embeddings used for deepfake detection. However, each modality is checked against an external reference of the claimed person, not against the other modality inside the same video, and there is no trajectory or drift modelling. It reports face reenactment as the hard case, because reenactment keeps the identity.

I.title: Voice-Face Homogeneity Tells Deepfake (VFD)
I.authors: Harry Cheng, Yangyang Guo, Tianyi Wang, Qi Li, Xiaojun Chang, Liqiang Nie
I.what_it_does: Voice-face matching network: transformer identity extractors for one face frame and a 3 s voice spectrogram, pre-trained on VoxCeleb2 with identity cross-entropy plus InfoNCE. It is fine-tuned on deepfake data with a real-fake contrastive loss, and a video is called fake when voice-face similarity falls below a threshold. Evaluated on DFDC, FakeAVCeleb and DeepfakeTIMIT. Note: arXiv v2 was withdrawn ('incorrect experiment setting'); v3 is the current version.
I.overlap_explanation: The original 'voice and face identity disagree' deepfake detector, so the cross-modal identity check itself is prior art. It is static (one random frame vs one 3 s clip), with no time windows, no trajectories and no drift comparison.

I.title: Referee: Reference-aware Audiovisual Deepfake Detection
I.authors: Hyemin Boo, Eunsang Lee, Jiyoung Lee
I.what_it_does: Synchformer audio-visual tokens over 8 segments go into an identity bottleneck with learnable queries. The target's identity tokens are cross-attended against a one-shot reference clip of the same speaker and trained with an identity-matching loss. An AV-Transformer then combines these identity tokens with synchrony cues. Trained on FakeAVCeleb; tested on FF++ (79.8 AUC) and KoDF (99.4 AUC).
I.overlap_explanation: Explicitly frames detection as cross-modal speaker-identity consistency ('verifying the correspondence between the speaker's voice and facial appearance'). It fuses identity jointly over audio and video, needs a reference clip, and does not model separate voice and face identity trajectories over time or their differential drift.

I.title: PIA: Deepfake Detection Using Phoneme-Temporal and Identity-Dynamic Analysis
I.authors: Soumyya Kanti Datta, Tanvi Ranga, Chengzhe Sun, Siwei Lyu
I.what_it_does: Audio-visual detector. WhisperX phonemes select frames; three streams (viseme crops, lip geometry, ArcFace identity embeddings) are fused with multi-head attention pooling. It adds an ArcFace temporal-consistency loss that penalizes 1 - cos(a_t, a_{t+1}) between consecutive frames (frame-to-frame identity drift). Evaluated on FakeAVCeleb and DeepSpeak v2.0.
I.overlap_explanation: Uses face-identity drift (a TI2Net-style consecutive-difference cue) inside an audio-visual detector, but audio enters only through phonemes and lip sync. No speaker-identity embeddings and no comparison between voice and face identity.

I.title: Identity-Driven Multimedia Forgery Detection via Reference Assistance (IDForge / R-MFDN)
I.authors: Junhao Xu, Jingjing Chen, Xue Song, Feng Han, Haijun Shan, Yu-Gang Jiang
I.what_it_does: New dataset of 54 celebrities with face-swap, lip-sync, voice-cloning and LLM-generated transcripts, plus a reference set of real clips. R-MFDN learns identity-aware features per modality (visual, audio, text) contrastively against same-identity reference clips, adds a cross-modal contrastive loss on clip-level features, and fuses everything for binary and multi-label classification.
I.overlap_explanation: Learns audio and visual features that are sensitive to identity, plus a cross-modal consistency loss. The identity check is against a reference set and at clip level; there is no per-window voice-vs-face identity trajectory or drift.

I.title: Synthetic Speech Detection Based on Temporal Consistency and Distribution of Speaker Features
I.authors: Yuxiang Zhang, Zhuo Li, Jingze Lu, Wenchao Wang, Pengyuan Zhang
I.what_it_does: Audio-only synthetic speech detector. Measures how consistent speaker-verification embeddings stay over time within one utterance (TTS speech is too consistent, VC speech differs), plus the distribution of speaker features across utterances.
I.overlap_explanation: This is essentially the audio half of Idea I: a voice-identity trajectory and its temporal consistency as a forensic cue, i.e. TI2Net's idea applied to speaker embeddings. It has no face stream and no cross-modal comparison. Cite it as prior art for the 'voice identity drift' component.

I.title: Detecting Deep-Fake Videos from Appearance and Behavior
I.authors: Shruti Agarwal, Tarek El-Gaaly, Hany Farid, Ser-Nam Lim
I.what_it_does: Biometric face-swap detector. Combines a static face-recognition embedding with a temporal behavioural embedding (expressions and head motion, learned with metric learning). A video is flagged when the two biometrics point to different identities.
I.overlap_explanation: Same detection logic (two identity signals that should agree, flagged on disagreement), but both signals are visual: appearance vs behaviour, not voice vs face. No speaker embeddings.

I.title: Deepfake audio detection by speaker verification
I.authors: Alessandro Pianese, Davide Cozzolino, Giovanni Poggi, Luisa Verdoliva
I.what_it_does: Detects synthetic speech using only the speaker's biometric characteristics: off-the-shelf speaker-verification embeddings compared against reference recordings of the claimed speaker, with no training on fakes.
I.overlap_explanation: Uses pretrained speaker-identity embeddings as the forensic signal, which is the audio component of Idea I. Audio-only and reference-based, with no face-identity trajectory.

I.title: Audio-Visual Activity Guided Cross-Modal Identity Association for Active Speaker Detection
I.venue_year: IEEE Open Journal of Signal Processing 2023 (arXiv 2022)
I.what_it_does: Unsupervised active speaker detection in movies and TV. Speech segments and face tracks are represented by speaker-identity and face-identity embeddings, and faces are assigned to speech by co-occurrence of identities across modalities over time, guided by audio-visual activity.
I.overlap_explanation: Adjacent field whose technique transfers directly: segment-level cross-modal association between speaker identity and face identity over a video's timeline. It is not used for forgery detection.

I.title: Deep Network Representations as Reliable Indicators of Synthetic Content in Audiovisual and Clinical Contexts
I.what_it_does: Interpretable indicator study on the DFRW dataset using ResNet, ViT, SlowFast, Wav2Vec2 and ECAPA-TDNN embeddings. Reports facial-embedding variance, Mahalanobis distance and audio-visual coherence as the strongest synthetic-content indicators.
I.overlap_explanation: Uses ECAPA speaker embeddings, the temporal variance of facial embeddings, and audio-visual coherence as hand-crafted indicators in one framework. Judged from the abstract only: no explicit voice-vs-face identity trajectory comparison is described. Lower-tier venue.

I.title: Not made for each other: Audio-Visual Dissonance-based Deepfake Detection and Localization
I.authors: Komal Chugh, Parul Gupta, Abhinav Dhall, Ramanathan Subramanian
I.what_it_does: Two-stream 3D-ResNet (video) plus MFCC CNN (audio), with a contrastive loss on 1 s chunks. The Modality Dissonance Score (mean audio-visual dissimilarity across chunks) is used for detection and temporal localization on DFDC and DeepFake-TIMIT.
I.overlap_explanation: Uses the same per-chunk audio-visual disagreement aggregated over time, but its features are generic or lip-sync features, not identity embeddings. Relevant as the template for windowed cross-modal dissonance scoring.

I.title: Seeing Voices and Hearing Faces: Cross-modal Biometric Matching
I.authors: Arsha Nagrani, Samuel Albanie, Andrew Zisserman
I.what_it_does: CNNs for binary and multi-way matching of a voice clip to the correct face (static or dynamic) and vice versa, trained on VoxCeleb and VGGFace.
I.overlap_explanation: The basic adjacent-field result showing that voice and face identity can be matched across modalities, which is the premise of Idea I. It is not a forensics paper and has no temporal drift.

I.title: Speaker Inconsistency Detection in Tampered Video
I.what_it_does: Detects audio replaced by another speaker's speech in talking videos (VidTIMIT, AMI, GRID), using lip-sync and dubbing detectors built on CNNs and RNNs, compared with classical classifiers.
I.overlap_explanation: Targets the same threat (voice not belonging to the person on screen) but detects it through lip-audio synchrony, not speaker-identity vs face-identity embeddings.

I.title: Combining Automatic Speaker Verification and Prosody Analysis for Synthetic Speech Detection
I.authors: Luigi Attorresi, Davide Salvi, Clara Borrelli, Paolo Bestagini, Stefano Tubaro
I.what_it_does: Synthetic speech detector that combines ASV speaker embeddings with a prosody encoder.
I.overlap_explanation: Uses speaker-identity embeddings as a deepfake cue, but audio-only and with no temporal-drift or face comparison.

I.title: Detecting Deepfake Talking Heads from Facial Biometric Anomalies
I.what_it_does: Flags deepfake talking-head impersonations (voice clone plus avatar, face-swap or lip-sync) from unnatural facial biometric patterns.
I.overlap_explanation: Biometric, person-centric detection of voice-cloned talking heads, but it relies on facial biometrics only; the voice identity is not compared with the face.

papers.title: Robust Deepfake Detection for Electronic Know Your Customer Systems Using Registered Images
papers.authors: Takuma Amada, Kazuya Kakizaki, Taiki Miyagawa, Akinori F. Ebihara, Kaede Shiohara, Toshihiko Yamasaki (NEC / Univ. Tokyo)
papers.what_it_does: This is a direct extension of TI2Net. It keeps TI2Net's Temporal Difference Comparison (consecutive identity-vector differences fed to an RNN, trained with CE + triplet + anchor-positive L2 loss). It adds an Auxiliary Difference Comparison: a stream of per-frame differences f(x_t) - f(x_registered) against a genuine enrolment image. The two streams are concatenated and passed to a bidirectional GRU (hidden size 1024). The face encoder is upgraded from ArcFace to ResNet100 AdaFace trained on WebFace12M. Training is on KoDF, and robustness is tested under blur, noise and JPEG.
papers.overlap_explanation: This paper explicitly calls itself a TI2Net upgrade. Its 'TDC only' ablation is TI2Net. Changes relative to TI2Net: (1) it needs a reference image, so it is no longer reference-free; (2) the encoder is swapped. That swap is a partial match to the 'replace ArcFace with a stronger face model' idea. It uses a larger supervised face-recognition model (AdaFace ResNet100 on WebFace12M), which helped a lot: cross-dataset CDF 50.8 -> 75.9 vs ResNet100-ArcFace. It does not use a self-supervised or fine-tuned face foundation model. (3) It keeps a GRU (bidirectional), not a transformer or Mamba. (4) It reports that random frame sampling generalises better than a sliding window, and that sequence length 4-64 changes AUC by up to about 7 points. That is a single-scale observation with no multi-scale self-similarity, so it does not cover B. The reference stream helps reenactment, but it does not do A (pose/expression-explained drift), F (real-only training or synthetic identity jitter), D (region-level trajectories) or I (voice-face). Retrained TI2Net reaches only CDF 64.2 / DFD 73.6 / DFDCp 61.0 here (KoDF-trained), which is a useful baseline citation.

papers.title: Unsupervised Multimodal Deepfake Detection Using Intra- and Cross-Modal Inconsistencies
papers.authors: Mulin Tian, Mahyar Khayatkhoei, Joe Mathai, Wael AbdAlmageed (USC ISI / Clemson)
papers.code_available: Not stated in the paper text read
papers.what_it_does: This is an unsupervised detector trained only on real VoxCeleb2 videos. Identity branch: per-frame AdaFace features are aggregated by a transformer encoder within fixed time windows. The whole network, including the pretrained AdaFace, is trained with a contrastive intra-modal identity-consistency loss across windows and identities. At test time it builds a T x T window-to-window identity similarity matrix and scores the video with a percentile of that matrix. A second, cross-modal branch (video features vs Whisper audio features) scores audio-visual synchronisation along the diagonal of a T x T matrix. The paper also gives an information-theoretic argument for a trade-off between motion and identity: a generator must either distort motion or leak identity.
papers.overlap_explanation: This is the closest prior art to several upgrade ideas. B: it already builds a temporal identity self-similarity matrix (T x T over windows), but at a single scale with a fixed window and a percentile score, not a learned multi-scale self-similarity matrix. F: it is already trained only on real videos, but it uses no synthetic identity-jitter fakes. Foundation-model swap: it already replaces ArcFace with AdaFace fine-tuned end-to-end. Transformer: it already uses a transformer, though only to pool frames inside a window. A: its theory links identity drift to motion, and it shows intra-modal AUC rises with motion magnitude, but it does not regress or explain identity drift with pose or expression. I: its cross-modal branch is lip/audio sync, not voice-identity vs face-identity consistency. D: none. FakeAVCeleb intra-modal (identity-only) AUC is 77.9, intra+cross is 96.8. It does not cite TI2Net.

papers.title: PIA: Deepfake Detection Using Phoneme-Temporal and Identity-Dynamic Analysis
papers.authors: Soumyya Kanti Datta, Tanvi Ranga, Chengzhe Sun, Siwei Lyu (University at Buffalo)
papers.venue_year: ICCV 2025 Workshops (APAI); arXiv 2510.14241 (Oct 2025); extended as T. Ranga MS thesis, UB tech report 2026-03
papers.what_it_does: This is an audio-visual detector with three streams: viseme mouth crops (3D CNN + EfficientNet-B0), lip-geometry mouth aspect ratio (MLP), and frozen ArcFace (InsightFace) identity embeddings encoded by an MLP. Frames are selected by WhisperX phoneme alignment (14 phonemes x 5 frames each). Streams are fused by multi-head attention pooling. An auxiliary 'ArcFace temporal consistency loss' (1 - cosine between adjacent frames, masked for silence) is added to CE. The paper motivates identity drift with consecutive-frame L2 spikes in face-swaps. Evaluated on FakeAVCeleb and DeepSpeak v2.0.
papers.overlap_explanation: This is a 2025 temporal-identity-drift paper, but identity is a minor stream: removing ArcFace costs only about 1 AUC point. Relative to TI2Net, identity drift becomes an auxiliary smoothness loss plus one input stream, and attention pooling replaces the GRU. That counts as transformer-style attention, but not over identity dynamics specifically. ArcFace stays frozen, so there is no foundation-model swap. A: no pose or expression conditioning. B: no self-similarity matrix. F: no real-only training or jitter synthesis. D: no region identity; mouth-region appearance is used, but not region identity. I: audio is used only as phonemes for frame selection and viseme matching, not as voice identity. Evaluated only in-domain and cross-manipulation on audio-visual datasets, not on the FF++ -> CDF protocol. It does not cite TI2Net.

papers.title: It Wasn't Me: Irregular Identity in Deepfake Videos
papers.authors: Honggu Liu, Paolo Bestagini, Lin Huang, Wenbo Zhou, Stefano Tubaro, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu
papers.what_it_does: This is a contemporaneous, independent take on the TI2Net idea. It observes that facial identity features are less stable over time in deepfakes, and trains a classifier on time series of per-frame face-recognition identity features (ArcFace, per the repository). It claims interpretability and robustness on low-quality (compressed) deepfakes, with promising cross-dataset results. Tested on FF++, Celeb-DF, FakeAVCeleb and VidTIMIT (from repository scripts).
papers.overlap_explanation: The core idea is the same as TI2Net: identity-feature time series classified for real vs fake. Based on the abstract and repository, it does not appear to add any of A, B, D, F or I. The exact temporal classifier could not be verified because the full paper text was not accessible; only the abstract and README were read. This is prior art that any 'temporal identity inconsistency' novelty claim must cite alongside TI2Net.

papers.title: Exploring Static-Dynamic ID Matching and Temporal Static ID Inconsistency for Generalizable Deepfake Detection
papers.authors: Huimin She, Yongjian Hu, Beibei Liu, Chang-Tsun Li
papers.what_it_does: This is a reference-free identity-anomaly detector with two branches. (1) A static-dynamic ID discrepancy branch checks a clip-level static ID (facial appearance) against a clip-level dynamic ID (facial behaviour). (2) A temporal static ID anomaly branch checks temporal inconsistency of per-image static IDs, which is TI2Net-like. Outputs are combined by weighted averaging. It adds a static-dynamic ID matching loss and a dynamic-ID constraint loss. The abstract claims it detects both face swap and face reenactment, generalises better to unknown datasets, and is robust to compression.
papers.overlap_explanation: This directly targets TI2Net's main weakness (reenactment) by adding a behaviour-based 'dynamic ID' branch next to the TI2Net-style temporal static-ID branch. That is related to, but not the same as, idea A. It checks whether appearance identity matches behavioural (motion) identity; it does not explain away appearance-identity drift using pose or expression. Only the abstract could be read because the Wiley/DOI full text failed to fetch, so backbone, temporal model and whether TI2Net is compared are unverified. Nothing in the abstract suggests B, D, F, I, Mamba, or a foundation-model swap.

papers.title: Detecting Deepfake Talking Heads from Facial Biometric Anomalies
papers.authors: Justin D. Norman, Hany Farid (UC Berkeley)
papers.what_it_does: This is an identity-agnostic, reference-free detector. It extracts ArcFace embeddings for every valid frame, discarding frames with head pitch > 25 deg or yaw/roll > 20 deg and occluded faces. It computes all N(N-1)/2 pairwise cosine similarities and summarises their distribution with 9 statistics (moments, quantiles, variance/mean and kurtosis/variance ratios). It classifies with XGBoost. It finds face-swap identity variation is either anomalously large or anomalously small (bimodal similarity distributions). It needs long videos (about 2000 or more frames). It fails cross-dataset (FaceFusion -> Celeb-DF 48% accuracy) and is sensitive to bitrate.
papers.overlap_explanation: Relative to TI2Net, it replaces consecutive differences + GRU with the distribution of the full pairwise identity self-similarity matrix. That is the closest existing use of an all-pairs identity self-similarity structure (relevant to B), but it is order-free statistics with no multi-scale or learned matrix encoder. A: pose is handled only by hard-thresholding frames (crude pose gating), not by explaining drift with pose or expression. The authors speculate that low-similarity frames come from difficult pose, lighting or expression, which supports A's motivation. No F, D or I. ArcFace is frozen; there is no transformer or Mamba. It does not cite TI2Net.

papers.title: In Anticipation of Perfect Deepfake: Identity-anchored Artifact-agnostic Detection under Rebalanced Deepfake Detection Protocol (ID-Miner)
papers.authors: Wei-Han Wang, Chin-Yuan Yeh, Hsi-Wen Chen, De-Nian Yang, Ming-Syan Chen (NTU / Academia Sinica)
papers.what_it_does: It proposes RDDP, a protocol where genuine videos are given the same deepfake artifacts via white-hat self-reenactment or surrogate noise. It also proposes ID-Miner: OpenFace facial-action-unit (FAU) sequences go into a frame encoder (artifact-agnostic contrastive loss), then a GRU aggregator with an identity-anchored contrastive loss. The model identifies the 'puppeteer' from action sequences and is used reference-based (cosine similarity to a reference video). TI2Net is a baseline.
papers.overlap_explanation: It cites and compares TI2Net, which degrades under RDDP. It moves from appearance identity (ArcFace) to behavioural identity (FAU dynamics), which targets reenactment. Its white-hat 'self-deepfakes' (real videos re-rendered with their own identity) are a form of synthetic training data built from real videos, a loose cousin of F, but not identity-jitter injection and not real-only training. It requires a reference video. It keeps a GRU. No pose/expression-explained ArcFace drift (A), no self-similarity matrix (B), no regions (D), no audio (I).

papers.title: Beyond Flicker: Detecting Kinematic Inconsistencies for Generalizable Deepfake Video Detection (KiMoI)
papers.authors: Alejandro Cobo, Roberto Valle, Jose M. Buenaposada, Luis Baumela (UPM / URJC)
papers.code_available: Not yet ('Code will be released upon publication')
papers.what_it_does: This is a pseudo-fake video generator trained only on pristine data. A transformer Landmark Perturbation Network decomposes landmark sequences into k=64 deformation bases. Gaussian noise on one basis over time breaks natural correlations between facial regions (for example eyebrow vs eyelid). The perturbed landmarks are rendered back into frames by Delaunay face morphing, then combined with SBI spatial pseudo-fakes. A MARLIN ViT encoder is trained on real + pseudo-fakes only. Video AUC from FF++: CDF 94.7, DFD 97.0, DFDCP 93.9, DFo 98.5. It is strong on the Wav2Lip reenactment subset.
papers.overlap_explanation: It does not use identity embeddings and does not cite TI2Net. It matters as prior art for idea F's 'real-only + synthetic temporal artifacts' recipe: it already shows real-only pseudo-fake video synthesis with structured, region-sampled temporal perturbations. Those perturbations are to landmark kinematics, not identity jitter. An identity-jitter generator (perturbing identity while keeping pose and expression) would be distinct, but reviewers will compare against KiMoI, VB, FakeSTormer and AltFreezing CBI. Its region sampling is a weak precedent for region-level temporal artifacts (D) in data synthesis, not in detection features.

papers.title: Referee: Reference-aware Audiovisual Deepfake Detection
papers.authors: Hyemin Boo, Eunsang Lee, Jiyoung Lee (Ewha Womans University)
papers.what_it_does: It uses Synchformer audio and visual encoders over 8 segments. An identity bottleneck with learnable queries compresses joint audio-visual tokens into speaker-identity tokens for the target and a one-shot reference clip. A cross-attention ID-matching module (with an identity-verification BCE loss) produces reference-aware identity tokens, which are fused with audio-visual tokens in an AV-Transformer for real/fake classification. Results: FakeAVCeleb 99.7 AUC, FF++ cross-dataset 79.8, KoDF 99.4.
papers.overlap_explanation: Relevant to idea I. It models cross-modal (voice+face) speaker identity consistency with transformers, but against a reference clip, and as segment-level tokens rather than an explicit voice-identity vs face-identity trajectory within one video. It has no ArcFace temporal differences and no pose/expression, self-similarity, region or jitter components. It does not cite TI2Net. A reference-free 'voice-ID(t) vs face-ID(t) consistency over time' design would still be distinct.

papers.title: Audio-Visual Person-of-Interest DeepFake Detection (POI-Forensics)
papers.authors: Davide Cozzolino, Alessandro Pianese, Matthias Niessner, Luisa Verdoliva
papers.what_it_does: Contrastive learning on real talking-head segments gives audio and video identity embeddings that characterise a person. At test time, segments are compared against a set of pristine reference videos of the person of interest. Inconsistency in either modality flags manipulation.
papers.overlap_explanation: This is prior art for idea I (audio-visual identity) and for real-only training (F, partially): training uses only real videos. It is person-of-interest and reference-based (Referee notes it needs minutes of reference footage), and it uses no temporal ArcFace drift, pose/expression conditioning, self-similarity or regions. Read via search abstract plus descriptions in Tian et al. and Referee; full text not read.

papers.title: Voice-Face Homogeneity Tells Deepfake
papers.authors: Harry Cheng, Yangyang Guo, Tianyi Wang, Qi Li, Xiaojun Chang, Liqiang Nie
papers.what_it_does: It detects deepfakes by voice-face matching. A model pre-trained on generic voice-face association data is fine-tuned to detect mismatch between a speaker's voice and face in fake videos.
papers.overlap_explanation: This is the main precedent for idea I (voice-face identity consistency), but it is a clip-level static voice-face match, not a time-resolved consistency between voice identity and face identity. It does not include TI2Net-style face identity dynamics. Abstract-level reading only.

papers.title: MARS: Multiscale Appearance-Residual Streams for Video Forgery Detection
papers.authors: Ahmed Y. Radwan, Shaina Raza (Vector Institute)
papers.code_available: Yes (project page / GitHub linked in paper)
papers.what_it_does: It is a full-frame detector on a frozen PE-Core-L encoder. A residual path applies fixed multiscale spatial and temporal difference-of-Gaussians to intermediate patch features and models them with a temporal transformer. A semantic path tunes LayerNorms only for frame classification, and a learned gate fuses the two. It reports seven-dataset average AUROC of 91.4, with transfer to generated video (GenVideo, DF26).
papers.overlap_explanation: It cites TI2Net only in related work as an example of modelling temporal changes in facial identity. It is relevant as a 2026 example of multi-scale temporal differencing with a transformer over foundation-model features. That is conceptually adjacent to B (multi-scale) and to the 'transformer + foundation model' upgrade, but it works on generic appearance features, not identity embeddings. No A, D, F or I.

papers.title: Interpretable Deepfake Detection in Videos via Explicit Forensic Features and Temporal Modeling
papers.authors: Chahira Benhama, Mohand Said Allili, Assia Hamadene (Univ. Quebec en Outaouais)
papers.what_it_does: It uses Kalman/Hungarian face tracking with an appearance-embedding cost to build identity-consistent face tracks. Each frame gets 68 handcrafted photometric, texture, geometric and compression descriptors, some computed on facial regions (mouth, jaw and hair boundary, left/right halves). A 2-layer LSTM over 20-frame windows does the classification.
papers.overlap_explanation: Identity is used only for tracking, not as the forensic signal. It has region-wise handcrafted features over time (weakly adjacent to D, but not identity), no TI2Net citation, and no A, B, F or I. Included because it surfaces under 'identity-consistent temporal' queries.

papers.title: UniForensics: Face Forgery Detection via General Facial Representation
papers.authors: Ziyuan Fang, Hanqing Zhao, Tianyi Wei, et al.
papers.what_it_does: It uses high-level semantic face features from a general facial representation model with a transformer-based video classifier to find temporal inconsistencies. It reports cross-dataset CDFv2 95.3 and DFDC 77.2.
papers.overlap_explanation: Relevant only to the 'foundation-model features + transformer over time' upgrade. Its features are general facial semantics, not identity, and identity dynamics are not modelled explicitly. Abstract-level reading only.

papers.title: Improving Generalization in Deepfake Detection with Face Foundation Models and Metric Learning
papers.authors: Stelios Mylonas, Symeon Papadopoulos (CERTH-ITI)
papers.venue_year: DHOW '25 workshop (ACM MM 2025); arXiv 2508.19730 (v2 withdrawn by authors)
papers.what_it_does: It fine-tunes the FSFM face foundation model (self-supervised on VGGFace2) frame by frame with CE + triplet loss (batch-all) on a 5-dataset mix. FSFM initialisation improves out-of-distribution performance on DF40 by about 7.6 AUC over ImageNet, including on reenactment.
papers.overlap_explanation: Note: the authors withdrew v2 of the arXiv preprint, so treat its findings with caution. It deliberately avoids temporal modelling. It is evidence that a fine-tuned face foundation model (FSFM) helps reenactment and out-of-distribution generalisation, which supports the 'swap ArcFace for a fine-tuned face foundation model' idea. It is not a temporal-identity method and does not cite TI2Net.

ti2net_citers.notes:
Scope: I found few papers that build directly on TI2Net. Only one is an explicit upgrade: the eKYC paper (NEC/UTokyo, FG 2025), which keeps the identity-difference + GRU + triplet design, adds differences against a registered (reference) image and swaps the encoder for AdaFace ResNet100/WebFace12M. Other works that cite or compare TI2Net mostly use it as a baseline or in related work: ID-Miner (2405.00483), MARS (2611.12508). Close independent or parallel temporal-identity works: It Wasn't Me (ICIP 2023), Tian et al. (2311.17088), She et al. (IET Biometrics 2024), PIA (ICCVW 2025), Norman & Farid (2507.08917).

Novelty mapping across what was found:
(A) Pose/expression-explained identity drift: NOT found. Closest are Norman & Farid (hard pose-threshold frame filtering), Tian et al. (theory of the motion-identity trade-off; AUC grows with motion) and She et al. (static appearance-ID vs dynamic behaviour-ID matching). None of them regress or condition ArcFace drift on pose or expression.
(B) Multi-scale identity self-similarity matrix: PARTIALLY pre-empted. Tian et al. already compute a single-scale T x T window-level identity similarity matrix (percentile score, unsupervised). Norman & Farid use statistics of the full pairwise ArcFace similarity distribution. No learned multi-scale self-similarity matrix encoder on identity embeddings was found. You must cite both and position against them.
(F) Real-only identity dynamics + synthetic identity-jitter videos: real-only identity training exists (Tian et al.; POI-Forensics). Real-only temporal pseudo-fakes exist for landmarks/kinematics (KiMoI 2512.04175, plus VB/FakeSTormer/AltFreezing CBI that it cites). Synthetic identity-jitter injection (perturbing identity while preserving pose and expression) was NOT found.
(D) Region-level identity trajectories: NOT found as identity. Only region-wise handcrafted features (2610.03380) and region-sampled landmark perturbation (KiMoI).
(I) Voice-face identity consistency over time: partially covered. Voice-Face Homogeneity (TOMM 2023, static matching), POI-Forensics (reference-based audio-visual identity) and Referee (2510.27475, reference-based audio-visual identity tokens with transformers). Tian et al. and PIA use audio for sync or phonemes, not voice identity. A reference-free, time-resolved voice-ID vs face-ID consistency signal appears open.
GRU -> transformer: Tian et al. (transformer over AdaFace features within windows); PIA (attention pooling). GRU -> Mamba on identity sequences: NOT found (Mamba deepfake papers exist but operate on pixel or CNN features).
ArcFace -> stronger or fine-tuned face model: eKYC (AdaFace WebFace12M, larger supervised face-recognition model, large gains) and Tian et al. (AdaFace fine-tuned end-to-end). A self-supervised face foundation model (FSFM, FaRL, MARLIN) used specifically for temporal identity was NOT found. FSFM and MARLIN are used frame-level or for generic features (2508.19730, which is withdrawn; KiMoI).

Tool issues: the Wiley/DOI full text for She et al. (IET Biometrics 2024) failed to fetch, so only the abstract was read and its comparison with TI2Net is unverified. The ICIP 2023 'It Wasn't Me' full text was not accessible; only the abstract and GitHub README were read, so its temporal classifier is unverified. Voice-Face Homogeneity, POI-Forensics and UniForensics were judged from SciSpace abstracts only. SciSpace, alphaXiv and WebSearch all worked otherwise. No Google Scholar 'cited-by' list was available, so the citing-paper list may be incomplete. SciSpace reports about 18-22 citations for TI2Net, and most of those not listed here appeared to be generic surveys or CNN-LSTM papers.

Video-level AUC, FF++ c23, Table 1: CDF-v2: 95.5, CDF-v3: 91.3, DFD: 97.5, DFDC: 86.8, DFDCP: 90.7. DF40, Table 2: face swap avg 95.9, face reenactment avg 86.1 (Wav2Lip 78.4, LIA 97.4, TPSM 82.4). papers.title: Can a World Model Predict a Deepfake Video? A Consistency Margin Prior for Deepfake Detection (ConsistencyNet)
papers.authors: Pradip Gupta, Shubham Mandloi, Ravi Kumar Satzoda, et al.
papers.what_it_does: Frozen V-JEPA 2.1 encoder with a LoRA-adapted predictor. The prediction residual is classified, with a margin loss that makes fake residuals larger than real ones. Video-level AUC, FF++, Table 1: CDF-v2: 90.5, DFDC: 87.1, DFDCP: 90.4, WildDF: 88.2, DE-2024: 66.4. DF40 face-swap avg: 95.5. Its Table 1 also cites (not opened by me) CDFA 97.2 / 83.8, DFD-HR 96.0 / 86.5, DiffusionFF 97.2 / 85.1, FakeRadar 91.7 / 84.1, DFF-Adapter 95.3 / 90.0 (CDF-v2 / DFDC).
papers.overlap_explanation: Temporal consistency through video-prediction residuals; conceptually close to a temporal-inconsistency signal.

papers.title: TwinD: Generalizing Deepfake Detection from Blending to Entire Face Synthesis
papers.authors: Andrii Yermakov, Jan Cech, Mario Fritz, Jiri Matas
papers.what_it_does: PE-core-L with LoRA, trained on FF++ fakes plus reconstruction and blob twins, with extra CCv2 reals. Re-runs 15 released detectors on its own face crops; video AUROC, Table 1. TwinD: DFD 98.9, FSh 96.8, CDFv2 97.1, FFIW 98.9, FAVC 99.9, CDFv3 90.4, DF26 95.8, 19-dataset avg 96.3. GenD-PE: CDFv2 95.9, FAVC 97.5, CDFv3 89.9. DFD-HR: 94.2 / 98.7 / 81.6. DFD-FCG (the only temporal model): 94.0 / 90.6 / 93.1. VLAForge: 95.0 / 94.5 / 72.4.
papers.overlap_explanation: Best numbers on FakeAVCeleb and Celeb-DF++, but on a non-standard protocol (own crops, extra real data).

papers.title: MARS: Multiscale Appearance-Residual Streams for Video Forgery Detection
papers.authors: Ahmed Y. Radwan, Shaina Raza
papers.what_it_does: Two-path video detector: difference-of-Gaussians residual streams plus a LayerNorm-tuned semantic path, with a gate. All baselines retrained for 3 epochs under a shared protocol. Video AUROC, FF++ c23 only: CelebDF 91.25, DF-TIMIT 99.85, UADFV 97.92, HiFiFace 84.92, GenVideo 93.99, DF26 75.50. Under this protocol, retrained ForAda reaches CelebDF 86.66 and GenD 66.13.
papers.overlap_explanation: Shows how much baseline numbers fall under a retrained shared protocol. Useful as a caveat for comparisons.

papers.title: SELFI: Selective Fusion of Identity for Generalizable Deepfake Detection
papers.authors: Younghun Kim, Minsuk Jang, Myung-Joon Kwon, Wonjun Lee, Changick Kim
papers.what_it_does: Frozen IResNet100 identity embedding, projected by a forgery-aware adapter, then fused with CLIP features through an identity relevance gate. FF++ c23. Frame-level AUC: CDFv2 0.839, DFD 0.907, DFDC 0.796, DFDCP 0.840. Video-level, Table 7: CDFv2 0.893, DFDC 0.820. Identity-only linear probe, frame AUC, Table 6: train DF -> test F2F 0.537, NT 0.519; train F2F -> F2F 0.826, DF 0.523.
papers.overlap_explanation: Identity-embedding detector. Shows that frozen face-recognition identity features transfer poorly from swaps to reenactment, the same failure seen in TI2Net.

TOOLS: alphaXiv worked; its answer_pdf_queries also read the CVF PDFs for TI2Net and TFCU. WebFetch on the CVF TI2Net PDF returned 403. I did not need SciSpace. Every number below was printed on a page I opened. Values cited through another paper's table are marked "via X".

SUMMARY TABLE. AUC %, train FF++ (c23/HQ unless noted), video-level unless noted. Columns: CDF2 | DFDC | DFD | DFo | FAVC | CDFv3 | DF40.
- TI2Net (WACV23; FF++ compression not stated): 68.22 | – | 72.03 | 76.08 | – | – | –. CDF1 66.65. DF->F2F 70.03.
- LipForensics (via TALL): 82.4 | 73.5 | – | 97.6. FSh 97.1.
- FTCN (via TALL/AltFreezing): 86.9 | 74.0 | 94.4 | 98.8. FSh 98.8.
- RealForensics (via TALL): 86.9 | 75.9 | – | 99.3. FSh 99.7.
- AltFreezing: 89.5 | – | 98.5 | 99.3. FSh 99.4. PwTF reproduces DFDC 74.7.
- TALL-Swin: 90.79 | 76.78 | – | 99.62. FSh 99.67.
- StyleFlow: 89.0 | – | 96.1 | 99.0. FSh 99.0. PwTF reproduces DFDC 70.8.
- NACO: 89.5 | 76.7 | – | 99.5. FSh 99.4.
- Pixel-wise TF (ICCV25): 89.7 | 75.2 | 97.3 | 99.4. FSh 99.3.
- TFCU (CVPR25): 93.18 | 86.05 | – | –. FFIW 91.27.
- FakeSTormer (ICCV25): 92.4 (T=16: 92.8) | 74.6 | 98.5 | –. DFDCP 90.0.
- DeepShield (ICCV25): 92.2 | 82.8 | 96.1 | –. DFDCP 93.2.
- VB-StA (CVPR25): 94.7 | 84.3 | 96.5 | 99.1. DFDCP 90.9. DF40 avg 94.2.
- DFD-FCG (CVPR25; DFDC subset): 95.0 | 81.8 | – | 99.6. FSh 98.1. FAVC 90.6 (GenD repro). CDFv3 93.1 (TwinD protocol). DF40 face-reenactment avg 81.8 (MoSTE).
- MoSTE (arXiv Nov 26): 95.5 | 86.8 | 97.5 | – | – | 91.3. DF40 face-swap avg 95.9, face-reenactment avg 86.1.
- ConsistencyNet (V-JEPA, Nov 26): 90.5 | 87.1 | – | –. DFDCP 90.4. DF40 face-swap avg 95.5.
- Frame-based foundation models, video AUC by frame averaging:
  - Effort: 95.6 | 84.3 | 96.5 | 97.7. DF40 avg 94.0.
  - ForAda: 95.7 | 87.2 | 97.2 | –. FAVC 93.1 (GenD repro).
  - GenD-CLIP: 96.0 | 87.1 | 97.0. FAVC 96.0, CDFv3 85.9.
  - GenD-PE: 95.8 | 81.6 | 96.5. FAVC 97.3, CDFv3 89.5.
  - VLAForge: 96.8 | 89.6 | 97.2.
  - TwinD (own crops + extra CCv2 reals): 97.1 | – | 98.9 | – | 99.9 | 90.4.
- Identity-based:
  - ID-Reveal (VoxCeleb-trained, needs reference videos): CelebDF 0.84, DFDCp 0.91.
  - SELFI (IResNet identity + CLIP): CDF2 89.3, DFDC 82.0 video-level.
  - ID-Miner protocol (not FF++): TI2Net FR 0.905, FS 0.877.

KEY POINTS FOR THE TI2NET UPGRADE:
1. Gap to close. TI2Net's 68.2 on CDF2 is about 20 points below the 2023-25 temporal specialists (89-93) and about 27 points below foundation-model detectors (95-97). TI2Net also never reported DFDC. Every strong 2024-26 paper reports CDF2 + DFDC (+ DFD, DFDCP), and increasingly FakeAVCeleb, Celeb-DF++ and DF40.
2. Reenactment transfer.
   - TI2Net DF->F2F is 70.0.
   - Under different protocols (not directly comparable to TI2Net): PwTF DF->F2F 75.0 (StyleFlow 63.0, FTCN 59.2); DeepShield DF->F2F 94.5.
   - SELFI's frozen-identity probe reaches only 0.537 from DF to F2F, which confirms that identity embeddings alone fail on reenactment.
   - The best DF40 face-reenactment average is MoSTE's 86.1.
3. StyleFlow (CVPR24) already upgrades the same latent-difference + GRU + contrastive/triplet recipe. It reaches CDF2 89.0, DFD 96.1, FSh 99.0, but the StyleGRU branch alone scores only CDF 62.5. So the sequence branch on its own is weak, and the gains come from fusing it with appearance (3D CNN) features. That is direct prior art for any upgrade built on identity differencing plus a GRU.

CAVEATS:
- DFDC subsets differ: DFD-FCG/RealForensics use 3,814 of 5,000 test videos; GenD uses roughly 2,500/2,500.
- CDF2 uses 518 test videos.
- Several "video-level" numbers come from frame models with averaged predictions.
- CDFA is printed as 93.8/83.0 in the Effort, MoSTE and VLAForge tables but as 97.2/83.8 in ConsistencyNet.
- MARS shows that retraining baselines under a shared 3-epoch protocol drops them sharply (ForAda CelebDF 86.7, GenD 66.1).
- TwinD uses its own crops and extra real data.
- 2508.19730 is withdrawn and trains on multiple datasets, so I excluded it. UVIF (2608.13064) uses a ForgeryNet/DFDCp protocol, not FF++, so I excluded it too.
